```{r setup, include=FALSE}
extrafont::loadfonts(quiet = TRUE)

# ── Register EB Garamond with R's graphics device ────────────────────────
# CSS alone cannot reach text rendered into ggplot SVG/PNG output. We
# register EB Garamond with R's font registry so any
# `family = "EB Garamond"` ggplot/ggiraph call renders correctly.
#
# Two-tier strategy (both defensive, both no-op cleanly if unavailable):
#   1. systemfonts::register_variant — aliases "EB Garamond" to an
#      installed serif so R has metrics for layout. ggiraph still emits
#      font-family="EB Garamond" in the SVG and the browser pairs it
#      with the Google Fonts webfont loaded via www/cssloaders.html.
#   2. showtext (optional) — if installed, also pull the real Google
#      Font so static raster output looks correct.
local({
  if (requireNamespace("systemfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
    have_eb <- "EB Garamond" %in% systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
    if (!have_eb) {
      candidates <- c("Garamond", "EB Garamond", "Georgia", "Times New Roman", "serif")
      installed  <- systemfonts::system_fonts()$family
      fallback   <- candidates[candidates %in% installed][1]
      if (!is.na(fallback)) {
        try(systemfonts::register_variant(
          name   = "EB Garamond",
          family = fallback
        ), silent = TRUE)
      }
    }
  }
  if (requireNamespace("showtext", quietly = TRUE) &&
      requireNamespace("sysfonts", quietly = TRUE)) {
    if (!"EB Garamond" %in% sysfonts::font_families()) {
      try(sysfonts::font_add_google("EB Garamond", "EB Garamond"),
          silent = TRUE)
    }
    try({
      showtext::showtext_auto()
      showtext::showtext_opts(dpi = 96)
    }, silent = TRUE)
  }
})

# ── Self-contained download icon ─────────────────────────────────────
# Shiny's downloadButton() defaults to a Font Awesome glyph
# (<i class="fa fa-download">). When the FA webfont fails to load, that
# glyph renders as a blank tofu square. dl_icon() supplies an inline SVG
# instead, wrapped in an <i> tag so it passes Shiny's validateIcon()
# check (which requires the icon tag name to be "i"). This removes the
# webfont dependency entirely, so the download affordance always renders.
dl_icon <- function() {
  tags$i(
    class = "dl-svg-icon", `aria-hidden` = "true",
    HTML(paste0(
      '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 16 16" ',
      'width="1em" height="1em" focusable="false" ',
      'style="vertical-align:-0.125em;margin-right:0.45em;fill:currentColor;">',
      '<path d="M8 1.5a.75.75 0 0 1 .75.75v6.69l2.22-2.22a.75.75 0 1 1 ',
      '1.06 1.06l-3.5 3.5a.75.75 0 0 1-1.06 0l-3.5-3.5a.75.75 0 1 1 ',
      '1.06-1.06l2.22 2.22V2.25A.75.75 0 0 1 8 1.5Z"/>',
      '<path d="M2.5 10.75a.75.75 0 0 0-1.5 0v1.75A1.75 1.75 0 0 0 2.75 ',
      '14.25h10.5A1.75 1.75 0 0 0 15 12.5v-1.75a.75.75 0 0 0-1.5 0v1.75a',
      '.25.25 0 0 1-.25.25H2.75a.25.25 0 0 1-.25-.25Z"/></svg>'
    ))
  )
}

east_coast_states_to_relocate <- c("RI", "DE", "DC", "MD")

us_states <- readRDS(here::here("data", "final", "us_states.Rds"))

#us_states <- states(cb = TRUE, resolution = "20m") %>%
  #shift_geometry() %>%
  #sf::st_cast("MULTIPOLYGON") %>% 
  #select(GEOID, ABBR = STUSPS, NAME, geometry)

us_states <- us_states %>% 
  left_join(
    us_states %>%
      sf::st_drop_geometry() %>%
      bind_cols(
        us_states %>%
          sf::st_centroid() %>%
          sf::st_coordinates() %>% 
          as_tibble()
      )
  ) %>% 
  mutate(
    x_lab = case_when(
      ABBR %in% east_coast_states_to_relocate ~ 2300000,
      ABBR == "FL" ~ X + 80000,
      ABBR == "LA" ~ X - 60000,
      .default = X
    ),
    y_lab = case_when(
      ABBR == "DC" ~ Y - 180000,
      ABBR == "DE" ~ Y + 100000,
      ABBR == "NH" ~ Y - 40000,
      ABBR == "VT" ~ Y + 40000,
      ABBR == "MD" ~ Y - 40000,
      ABBR == "LA" ~ Y + 40000,
      .default = Y
    )
  ) %>% 
  left_join(national_data)

### ----- Script sourcing helper -----
# Bare source() on a file missing from the deployment bundle fails with the
# opaque message "cannot open the connection", which says nothing about WHICH
# file is absent. On shinyapps.io that surfaces only as a stack trace in the
# logs. This helper checks first and names the offending path, along with the
# reason it is almost always missing: the file is not declared in the
# `resource_files:` block of this document's YAML header, so rsconnect never
# uploaded it. Run scripts/preflight_deploy.R before deploying to catch this
# locally instead of in production.
#
# `envir` must be an ENVIRONMENT, not TRUE/FALSE. Passing local = TRUE from
# inside this helper would evaluate the sourced file in the helper's own frame,
# and every object it defines would be discarded on return. Defaulting to
# parent.frame() reproduces what a top-level `source(..., local = TRUE)` does:
# evaluate in the caller's environment (here, the setup chunk).
source_required <- function(..., envir = parent.frame()) {
  path <- here::here(...)
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop(
      "Required script not found: ", path, "\n",
      "  If the app works locally but fails after deploy, this file is ",
      "probably missing from the `resource_files:` list in the YAML header ",
      "of ADA_PARC.Rmd. Add it, then redeploy.",
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }
  source(path, local = envir)
}

### ----- Functions import -----

source_required("scripts", "functions.R")

### ----- Tier palette import -----
# scripts/palettes.R is the single source of truth for ADA-PARC tier colour.
# Sourced into the GLOBAL environment (envir = globalenv()) rather than locally,
# because ADA_PARC_PALETTE and the pal_* accessors are read from inside Shiny
# reactives and render functions that do not share this chunk's environment.
# Nothing below should carry a tier hex literal. See docs/color-palette-expansion.qmd.
source_required("scripts", "palettes.R", envir = globalenv())

# The blue and slate chrome accent used to be patched in here, after
# palettes.R had been sourced, because palettes.R was shared with a second,
# still maroon copy of this document and could not be edited for one of them.
# That copy is gone and this document is canon, so the four tokens
# (ui_accent, ui_accent_dark, attr_text, attr_rule) now live in the standard
# set in scripts/palettes.R. Do not reintroduce a runtime override: values
# there are verified by `python3 scripts/check_palette.py` and mirrored in the
# fallback :root of www/styles.css, and a patch applied here is visible to
# neither.

### ----- Fixed city/place map classification -----
# City tract choropleth (output$snapshotmap) previously recomputed its color
# scale PER CITY (colorQuantile if >=4 tracts had data, else colorNumeric).
# That broke down for the many small/rural places with <4 tracts: 1-3 tract
# cities either got a non-4-step legend (colorNumeric + addLegend's default
# pretty()-based binning) or, for single-tract places, a blank legend (the
# domain collapses to one value, so addLegend's auto-computed cuts have
# length <= 1). See project memory "City Map Small-N Legend Bug".
#
# Fix: compute ONE fixed 4-category classification from the full national
# tract distribution (reusing the same create_non_overlapping_buckets() /
# format_ranges() helpers already used for the national state map), so every
# city's map is classified against the same breakpoints regardless of how
# many tracts that city has. This also makes colors comparable across
# different cities' maps, which per-city quantiles never allowed.
city_map_breaks <- create_non_overlapping_buckets(tracts_data$pct_cni_total_dis_place)
city_map_labels <- format_ranges(city_map_breaks, "pct_cni_total_dis_place")
```

# Home

```{r home}
# Embed logo as base64 data URI so the src resolves independently of Shiny's
# session URL context (relative paths like "PARC_blue_icon.png" can 404 when
# the browser resolves them against /session/ID/... rather than the app root).
#
# BRAND (provisional, 2026-08-04): www/brand holds the new identity pending
# approval from the ADA centers. Two blue-on-transparent files pair with two
# white-on-transparent files for dark surfaces:
#   PARC_blue_icon.png  / PARC_white_icon.png  384x384 square mark
#   PARC_blue_text.png  / PARC_white_text.png  448x264 two-line wordmark
# The hero carries both marks, mirroring the fact sheet banner adopted
# 2026-08-04 (fs_header() in factsheets/_generate/R/factsheet-functions.R):
# icon left, title block centred, wordmark right. The hero previously used the
# icon alone on the reasoning that the wordmark only repeats what the
# "Welcome to ADA-PARC" heading says; that was true of the words but not of
# the composition, and the home page and the fact sheets now open the same
# way. The BLUE files are used here, not the white ones, because the hero sits
# on the white page rather than on the navy banner.
logo_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(
  file = here::here("www", "brand", "PARC_blue_icon.png"),
  mime = "image/png"
)
wordmark_uri <- base64enc::dataURI(
  file = here::here("www", "brand", "PARC_blue_text.png"),
  mime = "image/png"
)

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* EB Garamond: declared here because shinyApp() sub-apps run in an
         isolated context where the parent flexdashboard www/styles.css
         does not reliably cascade into the rendered content. */
      *, *::before, *::after {
        box-sizing: border-box;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }
      /* ROOT FONT SIZE — read this before touching any rem value below.
         fluidPage() loads Bootstrap 3, whose scaffolding sets
         `html { font-size: 10px }`. Every rem on this page therefore
         resolved against a 10px root, which rendered 1.4rem body copy at
         14px and the contact line at 10.5px, roughly 62% of the intended
         size and well under the site's accessibility floor. Pinning the
         root here makes rem deterministic regardless of what Bootstrap
         version ships underneath, and every size below is expressed in
         rem against this 16px base (1.3125rem = 21px, matching the
         body size set in www/styles.css for the rest of the site). */
      html {
        font-size: 16px;
      }
      body, html {
        height: 100%;
        margin: 0;
        padding: 0;
        overflow-x: hidden;
        /* `auto`, not `scroll`: `scroll` paints a permanent scrollbar track
           even when the content fits. */
        overflow-y: auto;
        background: #f5f7fa;
      }
      .main-content {
        padding: 2.5rem 2.75rem 3rem 2.75rem;
        width: 100%;
        max-width: 1020px;
        margin: 0 auto;
        background: #ffffff;
        border-left: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-right: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        min-height: 100vh;
      }

      /* ---- Hero ---- */
      /* Three-column grid, matching .factsheet-header: mark left, title block
         centred, wordmark right. `auto 1fr auto` is what makes the middle
         column centre against the PAGE rather than against the space left
         over between the two marks, provided the two side columns end up
         near enough the same width. They do: the 72px square icon and the
         wordmark set to 60px tall on a 448x264 file (~102px wide) differ by
         about 30px, which is not readable as an offset at this width. A flex
         row with `flex: 1` on the text block, which is what this replaced,
         cannot centre at all: it centres the text inside whatever width is
         left, so the heading drifts left as the wordmark grows. */
      .home-hero {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 1.5rem;
        padding: 1.25rem 0 1.125rem 0;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 1.75rem;
      }
      .home-logo-wrap {
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      /* The brand icon is a 1:1 square, unlike the old wordmark it replaced,
         so height rather than width is the constraint that sets its visual
         weight. 72px reads level with the 32px hero heading; the old 96x64
         box would have shrunk a square mark to 64px and left it sitting
         light against the type. */
      .home-logo-wrap img {
        width: 72px;
        height: 72px;
        display: block;
      }
      /* Sized by HEIGHT, as on the fact sheet banner, so the two marks share
         an optical baseline. A width rule would set the height by accident,
         since the two files have different aspect ratios. */
      .home-wordmark {
        height: 60px;
        width: auto;
        display: block;
      }
      .hero-text-block {
        text-align: center;
        min-width: 0;
      }
      .welcome-text {
        font-size: 2rem;     /* 32px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.3rem 0;
        line-height: 1.15;
      }
      /* 19px, down from 20px. Below the 21px site body size, but this is a
         one-line standfirst under a 32px heading rather than reading copy,
         and it stays well clear of the 16px floor. #1c1c1c on #ffffff is
         17.4:1. */
      .welcome-sub {
        font-size: 1.1875rem; /* 19px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.4;
        margin: 0;
      }

      /* ---- Nav Cards ---- */
      /* Two columns, so four cards sit as a 2x2 block. Each card is wider
         than it was at three across, which is what lets the titles and
         descriptions carry the larger type without wrapping awkwardly. */
      .nav-cards {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
        gap: 1.125rem;
        margin-bottom: 2rem;
      }
      .nav-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-top: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 0 0 6px 6px;
        padding: 1.375rem 1.375rem 1.25rem 1.375rem;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        /* Centred, matching the hero above. `align-items: center` is what
           centres the icon tile and the button, which are flex ITEMS and so
           are unaffected by text-align; text-align centres the title and the
           description, which are text inside full-width items. Both rules
           are needed, and neither substitutes for the other. */
        align-items: center;
        text-align: center;
        transition: box-shadow 0.2s ease, transform 0.15s ease;
      }
      .nav-card:hover {
        box-shadow: 0 6px 20px rgba(28,43,58,0.12);
        transform: translateY(-2px);
      }
      /* Tile tint is #eef3fa, the palest usable step of the brand navy,
         replacing the maroon tint #fdf5f5 that paired with the old stroke.
         Not pure white: the card itself is white, so a white tile would
         erase the tile and leave the glyph floating. #eef3fa is 1.06:1
         against the card, enough to read as a shape, while the #013176
         stroke on it measures 11.07:1, comfortably past the 3:1 that
         non-text graphics require and past the 4.5:1 text floor as well. */
      .nav-card-icon {
        width: 50px;
        height: 50px;
        background: #eef3fa;
        border-radius: 8px;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        margin-bottom: 1rem;
        flex-shrink: 0;
      }
      .nav-card-icon svg {
        width: 26px;
        height: 26px;
        fill: none;
        stroke: #013176;
        stroke-width: 2;
        stroke-linecap: round;
        stroke-linejoin: round;
      }
      .nav-card-title {
        font-size: 1.3125rem;   /* 21px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
        line-height: 1.25;
      }
      .nav-card-desc {
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        flex-grow: 1;
      }
      /* Brand navy #013176, sampled from the tile fill of the PARC icon and
         defined as --brand-navy in factsheets/_generate/assets/factsheet-base.css.
         The jump-ahead buttons carry the identity colour rather than maroon so
         the one interactive element on the page is the one thing wearing the
         mark's blue; maroon stays on the structural rules (card top border,
         hero underline) and on the card icons. Hard-coded rather than
         referenced because this sub-app runs in an isolated shinyApp() context
         that the parent stylesheet's custom properties do not reach; if the
         approved brand shifts the blue, this literal and --brand-navy must
         move together.
         #ffffff on #013176 is 12.34:1. */
      .nav-card-btn {
        display: inline-block;
        padding: 0.55rem 1.2rem;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        background-color: #013176;
        border-radius: 4px;
        text-decoration: none !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.02em;
        transition: background-color 0.2s ease;
        cursor: pointer;
        border: none;
      }
      /* Gold on the darker blue is 6.6:1, so the hover state clears AA for
         normal text and does not depend on the 17px weight to pass. */
      .nav-card-btn:hover {
        background-color: #01214f;
        color: #C9A428 !important;
      }

      /* ---- Callout (full-width) ---- */
      .callout-full {
        border-left: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
        background: #f9f7f4;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 2rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .callout-label {
        font-size: 1rem;        /* 16px, uppercase with tracking */
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: 0.1em;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
      }
      .callout-text {
        font-size: 1.1875rem;   /* 19px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        font-weight: 500;
        margin: 0;
      }

      /* ---- Single-column sections ---- */
      .home-section {
        padding-bottom: 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.5rem;
        border-bottom: 0.5px solid #e4e8ef;
      }
      .home-section:last-of-type {
        border-bottom: none;
        margin-bottom: 0;
        padding-bottom: 0;
      }
      .sec-heading {
        font-size: 1.5rem;      /* 24px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.6rem 0;
        line-height: 1.25;
        border-left: 3px solid #1c2b3a;
        padding-left: 0.7rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .sec-body {
        font-size: 1.1875rem;   /* 19px */
        color: #2d3748;
        line-height: 1.7;
        margin: 0;
      }
      .sec-sub {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        margin-bottom: 0.6rem;
      }

      /* ---- Regions Grid ---- */
      .regions-grid {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
        gap: 0.2rem 2rem;
        margin: 0.75rem 0;
        list-style: none;
        padding: 0;
      }
      .regions-grid li {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */
        color: #2d3748;
        line-height: 1.55;
        padding: 4px 0;
      }
      .region-num {
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-right: 5px;
      }

      /* ---- Bottom Bar ---- */
      .bottom-bar {
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr;
        gap: 1.75rem;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1.5px solid #dfe3e9;
        border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 1.375rem 1.5rem;
        margin-top: 2rem;
      }
      .bottom-col-title {
        font-size: 1.25rem;     /* 20px */
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
        line-height: 1.25;
        border-left: 3px solid #1c2b3a;
        padding-left: 0.55rem;
        border-radius: 0;
      }
      .bottom-col-body {
        font-size: 1.0625rem;   /* 17px */
        color: #333333;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }
      /* Lead line of the authorship column, so the current maintainer reads
         as the primary credit and the historical contributors sit under it. */
      .bottom-col-lead {
        font-size: 1.125rem;    /* 18px */

      @media (max-width: 780px) {

        .home-logo-wrap, .home-wordmark { justify-self: center; }
        .regions-grid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
        .welcome-text { font-size: 1.75rem; }  /* 28px */
        .sec-heading { font-size: 1.3125rem; } /* 21px */
      }
    "))
  ),

  div(class = "main-content",

      # Hero
      # Icon carries alt="" because the wordmark to its right already names
      # the centre, and the heading names it a third time; announcing the
      # mark here would make a screen reader say "ADA-PARC" three times
      # before the first sentence of the page.
      div(class = "home-hero",
        div(class = "home-logo-wrap",
          tags$img(src = logo_uri, alt = "")
        ),
        div(class = "hero-text-block",
          div(class = "welcome-text", "Welcome to ADA-PARC"),
          div(class = "welcome-sub", "Tracking disability participation across the United States")
        ),

      ),

      # Navigation script: from the Home nav cards, jump to a top-level
      # flexdashboard page.
      #
      # Home renders as an embedded shinyApp(), so this code runs inside an
      # iframe that does not contain the navbar. Three paths are tried in
      # order, each independent of the last:
      #
      #   1. Direct: reach top.document and drive the navbar link. Only
      #      possible when parent and frame share an origin; throws otherwise.
      #   2. postMessage: hand the request to the listener installed in
      #      www/cssloaders.html, which runs in the document that owns the
      #      navbar. Works regardless of origin. This is the path that was
      #      missing, and the reason the cards did nothing.
      #   3. Hash: last resort, same-origin only.
      #
      # Every selector is scoped to the top navbar (.navbar-nav), so inner
      # tabsets such as the Scorecards tabset, and the scorecard/factsheet
      # iframes, can never be targeted by mistake.
      tags$script(HTML("
window.adaparcNavigateToTab = function(page) {
  var slugs = {
    'Home':          'home',
    'National Data': 'national-data',
    'City Data':     'city-data',
    'Scorecards':    'scorecards',
    'Scorecard':     'scorecards',
    'Fact Sheets':   'fact-sheets',
    'Help':          'help'
  };
  var slug = slugs[page];

  /* 1) Same-origin direct path. Any cross-origin access throws, which is
        caught here so the postMessage path below still runs. */
  try {
    var doc = top.document;
    void doc.documentElement;
    if (typeof top.adaparcShowPage === 'function') {
      if (top.adaparcShowPage(page)) { return true; }
    }
    if (slug) {
      var byHref = doc.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav a[href$=\\'#' + slug + '\\']');
      if (byHref.length) { byHref[0].click(); return true; }
    }
    var links = doc.querySelectorAll('.navbar-nav a');
    for (var i = 0; i < links.length; i++) {
      if ((links[i].textContent || '').trim() === page) { links[i].click(); return true; }
    }
  } catch (e) { /* fall through to postMessage */ }

  /* 2) Cross-origin safe path. The listener lives in www/cssloaders.html. */
  try {
    var target = (window.parent && window.parent !== window) ? window.parent : top;
    target.postMessage({ adaparc: 'navigate', page: page }, '*');
    return true;
  } catch (e) {}

  /* 3) Last resort. */
  if (slug) {
    try { top.location.hash = '#' + slug; return true; } catch (e) {}
  }
  return false;
};
      ")),

          ),

        )
      ),

      # Single-column sections
      div(class = "home-section",
        div(class = "sec-heading", "What is the ADA?"),
        tags$p(class = "sec-body",
          "The Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), established in 1990, is a landmark civil rights law that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in all areas of public life.",
          " Since the ADA, organizations across public and private sectors have worked to improve the quality of life for individuals with disabilities in the U.S. ADA-PARC emphasizes key components of Census and HUD data to shed light on the lived experiences and outcomes for people with disabilities."
        )
```

# National Data

```{r National Data}
library(shiny)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(shinycssloaders)
library(DT)
library(ggiraph)

# Build grouped <optgroup> choices for the "Select a topic" <select>. The group
# heading is the text before the first ":" in national_dropdown_label; the
# option VALUE stays the full label (the National Data server maps that label
# to a var_readable downstream), while the visible option text is only the part
# after the colon so the heading is not repeated on every row. Labels with no
# colon (e.g. "People with Disabilities") render as ungrouped options first, in
# dict_vars row order.
nat_topic_choices <- function(cat_col) {
  labs <- dict_vars %>%
    dplyr::filter(.data[[cat_col]] == TRUE, !is.na(national_dropdown_label)) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(national_dropdown_label) %>%
    dplyr::pull(national_dropdown_label)

  has_grp <- grepl(":", labs, fixed = TRUE)
  grp <- ifelse(has_grp, trimws(sub(":.*$", "", labs)), "")
  opt <- ifelse(has_grp, trimws(sub("^[^:]*:\\s*", "", labs)), labs)

  out <- list()
  for (g in unique(grp)) {
    i <- which(grp == g)
    if (identical(g, "")) {
      for (k in i) out[[opt[k]]] <- labs[k]
    } else {
      out[[g]] <- stats::setNames(as.list(labs[i]), opt[i])
    }
  }
  out
}

# Default topic label for a category ("People with Disabilities" when present,
# else the first topic in dict_vars order). Marks the checked radio whenever the
# topic list (re)renders on a category change.
nat_topic_default <- function(cat_col) {
  flat <- unlist(nat_topic_choices(cat_col), use.names = FALSE)
  if ("People with Disabilities" %in% flat) "People with Disabilities" else flat[[1]]
}

# Grouped radio list for the collapsible topic picker. Real
# <input type="radio" name="national_variable_selector"> elements, so Shiny's own
# radio input binding carries the selection; each option VALUE is the full
# national_dropdown_label (mapped to var_readable downstream) and the visible
# text is only the part after the group's colon.
#
# Each visual group is wrapped in <div role="group" aria-labelledby=heading-id>
# so a screen reader announces "Employment" (etc.) on entry rather than reading
# a flat list of leaf labels with no context. Shiny's radio binding queries
# radios by name across all descendants, so the extra wrapper is transparent to
# it; the sticky .ntt-group-head still pins to the scroll container's top.
nat_topic_radios <- function(cat_col, selected) {
  grp  <- nat_topic_choices(cat_col)
  kids <- list()
  mk_row <- function(text, value) {
    on <- identical(value, selected)
    tags$div(
      class = "ntt-row",
      tags$label(
        class = "ntt-row-label",
        tags$input(
          type    = "radio",
          class   = "ntt-radio",
          name    = "national_variable_selector",
          value   = value,
          checked = if (on) "checked"
        ),
        tags$span(class = "ntt-dot", `aria-hidden` = "true"),
        tags$span(class = "ntt-row-text", text)
      )
    )
  }
  for (nm in names(grp)) {
    v <- grp[[nm]]
    if (is.list(v)) {
      head_id <- paste0("ntt-grp-", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(nm)))
      kids[[length(kids) + 1]] <- tags$div(
        class = "ntt-group",
        role  = "group",
        `aria-labelledby` = head_id,
        tags$div(class = "ntt-group-head", id = head_id, nm),
        lapply(names(v), function(leaf) mk_row(leaf, v[[leaf]]))
      )
    } else {
      kids[[length(kids) + 1]] <- mk_row(nm, v)
    }
  }
  tags$div(
    id = "national_variable_selector",
    class = "shiny-input-radiogroup shiny-input-container ntt-list",
    role = "radiogroup",
    # Point at the visible field label rather than repeat the string, so the
    # group name can't drift out of sync with it.
    `aria-labelledby` = "national-topic-label",
    kids
  )
}

ui <- fluidPage(

      .table_national {
        width: 100%;

        font-size: 19px;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.8rem 0;
        line-height: 1.25;
      }
      .understanding-chip {
        flex: none;
        width: 40px;
        height: 40px;
        border-radius: 50%;
        background: #1c2b3a;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
      }
      .understanding-glyph {
        width: 21px;
        height: 21px;
        fill: none;
        stroke: #ffffff;
        stroke-width: 1.7;
        stroke-linecap: round;
        stroke-linejoin: round;
      }
      .understanding-body {
        font-size: 16px;
        line-height: 1.62;
        color: #28394a;
        margin: 0;
        max-width: 74ch;
      }
      /* One definition per row: term, then its plain-language meaning directly
         beneath it, hairline-separated so the list stays scannable. */
      .understanding-defs { margin: 0.15rem 0 0 0; }
      .understanding-def {
        padding: 0.85rem 0;
        border-top: 1px solid #d5dee8;
      }
      .understanding-def:first-child { padding-top: 0.35rem; border-top: 0; }
      .understanding-def:last-child { padding-bottom: 0.15rem; }
      .understanding-def dt {
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 16px;
      }
      .understanding-def dd {
        margin: 0.28rem 0 0 0;
        font-size: 16px;
        line-height: 1.55;
        color: #28394a;
        max-width: 74ch;
      }
      .understanding-defs-note {
        font-size: 15px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #d5dee8;
        border-left: 3px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 4px;
        padding: 0.7rem 0.95rem;
        margin: 1rem 0 0 0;
      }

      /* ── National controls panel ─────────────────────────────────────────
         One horizontal band: the two selectors on the left, the download on
         the right behind a full-height vertical rule. The topic summary lives
         in its own card below so nothing competes for width here. */
      .national-controls-split {
        display: flex;
        align-items: stretch;
        gap: 1.5rem;
      }

      /* Selector row: align-items:flex-start keeps the two labels on the same
         baseline. Bottom alignment used to push the shorter control down
         whenever a long topic name wrapped the second select box onto two
         lines. */
      .national-controls-row {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        min-width: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
        align-items: flex-start;
        gap: 1.25rem;
      }
      .national-control-field {
        flex: 1 1 16rem;
        min-width: 0;
      }
      /* Shiny wraps selectInput in .form-group with a bottom margin; zeroing
         it lets align-items:flex-end line the controls up exactly. */
      .national-control-field .form-group {
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }
      /* The download sits in its own full-height column, set off by a hairline
         rule so it reads as a separate action rather than a third control. */
      .national-control-action {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        border-left: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
        padding-left: 1.5rem;
      }

      /* Download button: the single primary action on this tab. Solid navy,
         white label (12.34:1), generous target, shape + radius + focus ring
         consistent with the category buttons. Sized in px, not rem: this
         fluidPage() resolves rem against a 10px Bootstrap-3 root, which is
         why the label read tiny before. */
      .btn-download-national {
        display: inline-flex !important;
        align-items: center !important;
        justify-content: center !important;
        min-height: 48px !important;
        padding: 12px 30px !important;
        background: #013176 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #013176 !important;
        border-radius: 7px !important;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 18px !important;
        font-weight: 600 !important;
        line-height: 1.2 !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.01em !important;
        white-space: nowrap !important;
        text-align: center !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        transition: background-color .12s ease, border-color .12s ease !important;
      }
      .btn-download-national:hover {
        background: #01214f !important;
        border-color: #01214f !important;
      }
      .btn-download-national:focus,
      .btn-download-national:focus-visible {
        /* #0d3b8e is almost the button's own #013176 navy, so the ring reads as
           a fatter edge, not a focus indicator. Dark ink ring (~14:1 on white)
           + a 3px white halo so it separates from the fill on any background. */
        outline: 3px solid #1c2b3a !important;
        outline-offset: 3px !important;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #ffffff !important;
      }
      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
        .btn-download-national { transition: none !important; }
      }
      /* Narrow screens: stack the columns and turn the vertical rule into a
         horizontal one above the button. */
      @media (max-width: 900px) {
        .national-controls-split {
          flex-wrap: wrap;
        }
        .national-control-action {
          flex: 1 1 100%;
          justify-content: flex-start;
          border-left: none;
          border-top: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
          padding-left: 0;
          padding-top: 1rem;
        }
        .national-control-field .form-group {
          margin-bottom: 0.25rem;
        }
      }

      /* Category = segmented control, Topic = grouped native select.
         The category picker is radioGroupButtons() (real radio inputs inside
         btn/btn-national-cat labels), so arrow-key navigation within the group
         is native. The topic picker is a native select (selectize = FALSE) so
         optgroup headings, the mobile OS picker and screen-reader semantics all
         work with no extra wiring. Focus rings match .btn-download-national
         (3px #0d3b8e + white halo). */
      .national-controls-stack {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        min-width: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        gap: 1rem;
      }
      .national-controls-stack .national-cat-field,
      .national-controls-stack .national-control-field {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
      }
      .national-cat-field .form-group,
      .national-control-field .form-group {
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }
      .national-cat-field .control-label,
      .national-control-field .control-label,
      .national-control-field > .shiny-input-container > label,
      .national-control-field label.control-label {
        display: block;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
      }

      /* Segmented category buttons. shinyWidgets radioGroupButtons renders a
         btn.radiobtn.btn-national-cat <button> (with a hidden radio inside)
         per item, wrapped in .btn-group-toggle, all inside
         .btn-group-container-sw. */
      .national-cat-field br { display: none; }
      .national-cat-field .btn-group-container-sw {
        display: flex;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
        gap: 8px;
        width: 100%;
      }
      .national-cat-field .btn-group-container-sw > .btn-group-toggle {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        display: flex;
      }
      .btn.btn-national-cat {
        width: 100%;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 16px;
        font-weight: 600;
        line-height: 1.3;
        min-height: 44px;
        padding: 10px 16px;
        margin: 0;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        background: #f2f0ec;
        border: 1.5px solid #c9c0ac;
        border-radius: 6px;
        cursor: pointer;
        white-space: normal;
        transition: background-color .12s ease, border-color .12s ease;
      }
      .btn.btn-national-cat:hover {
        background: #e7e2d6;
        border-color: #1c2b3a;
      }
      /* Selected state: shinyWidgets adds .active to the button; :has() is the
         fallback for when a keyboard arrow-change doesn't fire Bootstrap's
         .active sync (e.g. Firefox). */
      .btn.btn-national-cat.active,
      .btn.btn-national-cat:has(> input:checked) {
        background: #013176;
        border-color: #013176;
        color: #ffffff;
        box-shadow: none;
      }
      /* Focus lands on the visually-hidden radio -> show the ring on the
         button, matching .btn-download-national. */
      .btn.btn-national-cat:focus-within {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e;
        outline-offset: 2px;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff;
      }
      /* Selected button is #013176 navy; the #0d3b8e focus token is nearly the
         same blue, so the ring vanishes into the fill. Swap to the dark ink ring
         (14:1 on white, well clear of the navy) with a 3px white halo so the
         indicator reads on every category state. */
      .btn.btn-national-cat.active:focus-within {
        outline-color: #1c2b3a;
        outline-offset: 3px;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #ffffff;
      }
      .btn-national-cat > input[type=radio] {
        position: absolute;
        width: 1px;
        height: 1px;
        opacity: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
      }

      /* Collapsible topic picker: disclosure button + grouped radio list.
         The trigger echoes .btn-national-cat; the list is the inline Option A
         list, revealed in the page flow (no floating layer). */
      .national-topic-field .field-label-text {
        display: block;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
      }
      .national-topic-toggle {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: space-between;
        gap: 10px;
        width: 100%;
        min-height: 46px;
        padding: 10px 14px;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        font-weight: 500;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1.5px solid #8a8a8a;
        border-radius: 7px;
        cursor: pointer;
        text-align: left;
      }
      .national-topic-toggle:hover { border-color: #1c2b3a; }
      .national-topic-toggle:focus-visible {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e;
        outline-offset: 2px;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px #ffffff;
      }
      .national-topic-toggle .ntt-value {
        overflow: hidden;
        text-overflow: ellipsis;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      .national-topic-toggle .ntt-value .shiny-text-output { white-space: nowrap; }
      .national-topic-toggle .ntt-caret {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
        width: 11px; height: 11px;
        border-right: 2px solid #4a4a4a;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #4a4a4a;
        transform: rotate(45deg) translate(-2px, -2px);
      }
      .national-topic-toggle[aria-expanded=true] .ntt-caret {
        transform: rotate(-135deg) translate(-1px, -1px);
      }

      .national-topic-region { display: grid; grid-template-rows: 1fr; }
      .national-topic-region.is-collapsed { grid-template-rows: 0fr; }
      .national-topic-region > .national-topic-clip { overflow: hidden; min-height: 0; }
      .national-topic-region.is-collapsed > .national-topic-clip { visibility: hidden; }

      .ntt-list {
        margin-top: 8px;
        max-height: 320px;
        overflow-y: auto;
        /* Don't let a wheel/trackpad scroll that reaches the end of the list
           chain out and scroll the whole page. */
        overscroll-behavior: contain;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1.5px solid #8a8a8a;
        border-radius: 7px;
        padding: 4px 0 6px;
      }
      .ntt-group-head {
        position: sticky;
        top: 0;
        background: #f2f0ec;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 12px;
        font-weight: 700;
        letter-spacing: 0.06em;
        text-transform: uppercase;
        color: #55503f;
        padding: 7px 16px 5px;
        border-bottom: 1px solid #e0d9c7;
        z-index: 1;
      }
      .ntt-row { border-left: 3px solid transparent; }
      .ntt-row + .ntt-row { border-top: 1px solid #efeadd; }
      .ntt-row-label {
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        gap: 11px;
        margin: 0;
        /* ~44px row so the pointer/touch target clears the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum */
        padding: 12px 16px 12px 13px;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 17px;
        font-weight: 400;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        cursor: pointer;
      }
      .ntt-radio {
        position: absolute;
        width: 1px; height: 1px;
        opacity: 0;
        pointer-events: none;
      }
      .ntt-dot {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
        width: 16px; height: 16px;
        border-radius: 50%;
        border: 1.5px solid #8a8a8a;
        background: #ffffff;
        display: grid;
        place-items: center;
      }
      .ntt-dot::after {
        content: '';
        width: 8px; height: 8px;
        border-radius: 50%;
        background: #013176;
        transform: scale(0);
      }
      .ntt-row:hover { background: #f1eee6; }
      .ntt-radio:checked ~ .ntt-dot { border-color: #013176; }
      .ntt-radio:checked ~ .ntt-dot::after { transform: scale(1); }
      .ntt-radio:checked ~ .ntt-row-text { font-weight: 600; }
      .ntt-radio:focus-visible ~ .ntt-dot {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e;
        outline-offset: 2px;
      }
      /* Progressive enhancement: tint the whole row that holds the checked
         radio (browsers without :has() still show the filled dot + bold text). */
      .ntt-row:has(.ntt-radio:checked) {
        background: #eef2f8;
        border-left-color: #013176;
      }
      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) {
        .national-topic-region { transition: grid-template-rows .18s ease; }
        .ntt-dot::after { transition: transform .12s ease; }
        .national-topic-toggle .ntt-caret { transition: transform .15s ease; }
      }

      /* Visually hidden but announced (clip pattern, not display:none). */
      .nat-sr-only {
        position: absolute;
        width: 1px;
        height: 1px;
        padding: 0;
        margin: -1px;
        overflow: hidden;
        clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
        clip-path: inset(50%);
        white-space: nowrap;
        border: 0;
      }

      /* Narrow screens: one category button per row. */
      @media (max-width: 760px) {
        .national-cat-field .btn-group-container-sw > .btn-group-toggle {
          flex: 1 1 100%;
        }
      }
      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
        .btn.btn-national-cat { transition: none; }
      }

      /* Length + search controls: left-aligned with some spacing */
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_length,
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_filter {
        float: left;
        text-align: left;
        margin-right: 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
      }
      div.dataTables_wrapper div.dataTables_filter label {
        white-space: nowrap;
      }

      /* DT Buttons download button */
      .dt-buttons {
        float: left;
        margin-right: 1rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.5rem;
      }
      .dt-button {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 1rem !important;
        font-weight: 600 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        background: #013176 !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #013176 !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        padding: 4px 14px !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        line-height: 1.5 !important;
      }
      .dt-button:hover {
        background: #01214f !important;
        border-color: #01214f !important;
      }
      .dt-button:focus {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e !important;
        outline-offset: 2px !important;
      }

      /* ── National Data: card layout ───────────────────────────────────────── */

      /* Page header — warm beige background, maroon heading.
         Sized in px, not rem: this is a fluidPage(), so Bootstrap 3
         scaffolding sets `html { font-size: 10px }` and every rem here
         resolves against a 10px root. The old `1rem 1.5rem` padding was
         therefore 10px/15px and the `2.6rem` heading only 26px, which is
         why the band read as cramped. */
      .national-banner {
        background: #f9f7f4;
        border-bottom: 3px solid #e8e4db;
        padding: 20px 24px 18px;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0;
      }
      .national-banner h1 {
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 31px;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-bottom: 6px;
      }
      .national-banner .national-intro {
        color: #2c2c2c;
        margin-top: 0;
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }

      /* Base card */
      .national-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-radius: 8px;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem 1.5rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(28, 43, 58, 0.07);
      }

      /* Maroon accent on top edge of each card */
      .national-controls-card,
      .national-map-card,
      .national-table-card {
        border-top: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* The map card carries more inside room than the other cards: the
         figure is the centrepiece of this tab and was sitting tight against
         the card edges. Paired with the taller girafe canvas below
         (height_svg 5 -> 6), which is what actually enlarges the map. */
      .national-map-card {
        padding: 18px 22px 26px 22px;
      }

      /* Topic summary band: its own space between the controls and the map.
         Kept lighter than the other cards (gold left rule, no maroon top bar,
         warm tint) so it reads as explanatory prose, not a fourth panel. */
      .national-summary-card {
        background: #fbf8f2;
        border: 1px solid #e6dcc6;
        border-left: 4px solid #c8a743;
        box-shadow: none;
        padding: 1.15rem 1.5rem;
      }
      /* Spans the full card width. The former `max-width: 78ch` capped the
         measure at roughly half the card and pushed the summary into a tall
         narrow column, leaving the right side of the band empty. The band is
         two or three sentences, so the taller-than-ideal measure costs less
         than the vertical space the cap was consuming. */
      .national-summary-card .map-summary {
        display: block;
        line-height: 1.55;
      }
      .national-summary-heading {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 19px;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin: 0 0 0.4rem 0;
        line-height: 1.3;
      }

      /* Sort arrow contrast: DataTables sets opacity:0.125 on ::before/::after;
         using table.dataTable.table_national gives higher specificity than
         DataTables own selectors so !important is not needed on most rules.
         Partial opacity was the reason the arrows read as grey: white at 0.6
         over the slate header resolves to a mid grey. Every arrow is now solid
         white at full opacity, and the active sort direction is picked out in
         gold so the sorted state is still obvious. */
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc {
        background-image: none !important;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting::after,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::after,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::after {
        opacity: 1 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        font-size: 14px !important;
        line-height: 11px !important;
        right: 9px !important;
      }
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_asc::before,
      table.dataTable.table_national thead th.sorting_desc::after {
        color: #f2c75c !important;   /* gold: active direction, 8.7:1 on slate */
      }
    "))
  ),

  tags$main(
    role = "main",

    # ── Page header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-banner",
      h1("National Data"),
      tags$p(
        class = "national-intro",
        "Pick a category, then a topic; the map, summary, and table update to match. The Download button gives a print-ready report of the current topic: map and key on page one, full state table on page two."
      )
    ),

    # ── Controls card ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-controls-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "Data selection controls",
        # Single horizontal row: the two selectors on the left, the download on
        # the right behind a vertical rule. The topic summary is no longer part
        # of this card; it sits in its own card below. Stacks under 900px.
        div(
          class = "national-controls-split",
          div(
            class = "national-controls-stack",
            div(
              class = "national-cat-field",
              radioGroupButtons(
                inputId  = "national_category_selector",
                label    = "Select a category",
                choices  = c(
                  "Demographics",
                  "Community Living",
                  "Community Participation",
                  "Work/Economic"
                ),
                selected = "Demographics",
                status   = "national-cat",
                size     = "normal"
              )
            ),
            div(
              class = "national-control-field national-topic-field",
              tags$span(
                class = "field-label-text",
                id    = "national-topic-label",
                "Select a topic"
              ),
              tags$button(
                type              = "button",
                id                = "national-topic-toggle",
                class             = "national-topic-toggle",
                `aria-expanded`   = "false",
                `aria-controls`   = "national-topic-region",
                `aria-labelledby` = "national-topic-label national_topic_current",
                tags$span(
                  class = "ntt-value",
                  textOutput("national_topic_current", inline = TRUE)
                ),
                tags$span(class = "ntt-caret", `aria-hidden` = "true")
              ),
              tags$div(
                id    = "national-topic-region",
                class = "national-topic-region is-collapsed",
                tags$div(
                  class = "national-topic-clip",
                  uiOutput("national_topic_group")
                )
              )
            )
          ),
          # Visually hidden live region: names the active category, how many
          # topics it has, and the topic now shown. Worded differently from the
          # map-summary live region so the two don't read on top of each other.
          div(
            class = "nat-sr-only",
            role  = "status",
            `aria-live` = "polite",
            textOutput("national_selection_status", inline = TRUE)
          ),
          div(
            class = "national-control-action",
            downloadButton(
              "download_national_topic",
              "Download",
              class        = "btn-download-national",
              icon         = dl_icon(),
              `aria-label` = "Download a print-ready report of the current topic"
            )
          )
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Topic summary card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Given its own full-width band between the controls and the map so the
    # definition/high-low sentence reads as prose rather than as a caption
    # squeezed beside the controls.
    div(
      class = "national-card national-summary-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-labelledby` = "national-summary-heading",
        h2(
          "About This Topic",
          id    = "national-summary-heading",
          class = "national-summary-heading"
        ),
        div(
          `aria-live` = "polite",
          uiOutput("national_map_summary") %>% withSpinner()
        )
        # "Population examined" now lives in the "Understanding This Data" card
        # below the table, alongside the source and column definitions.
      )
    ),

    # ── Map card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-map-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "Selected topic title",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_map_title") %>% withSpinner()
      ),
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "How to read the map",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_map_note")
      ),
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "State-by-state map of selected topic",
        div(
          id           = "national_map_img",
          role         = "img",
          `aria-label` = "Map of the United States. Use the topic dropdown to select a variable.",
          # Height tracks the girafe canvas aspect. opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE,
          # width = 1) scales the SVG to the container WIDTH and derives its
          # height from the width_svg:height_svg ratio, so this value only has
          # to be a container tall enough not to clip. At 10:6 a ~900px card
          # renders the figure about 540px tall.
          girafeOutput("national_ggmap", width = "100%", height = "560px") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # Tiny JS handler: updates the map div's aria-label reactively
    tags$script(HTML("
      Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('updateMapAriaLabel', function(x) {
        var el = document.getElementById('national_map_img');
        if (el) el.setAttribute('aria-label', x.label);
      });
    ")),

    # ── Table card ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "national-card national-table-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-label` = "Data table for selected topic",
        `aria-live` = "polite",
        uiOutput("national_table_title"),
        div(
          class = "table-container",
          uiOutput("national_table") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Understanding This Data ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    # One reference card below the table: who is counted (universe_note), where
    # the numbers come from (data_source_label), and what each percentage column
    # means (pct_definition). Built as a single output so it refreshes atomically
    # and stays in lockstep with the downloaded report (national_topic.qmd).
    div(
      class = "national-card national-understanding-card",
      tags$section(
        `aria-labelledby` = "national-understanding-heading",
        h2(
          "Understanding This Data",
          id    = "national-understanding-heading",
          class = "national-understanding-heading"
        ),
        div(class = "understanding-rule", `aria-hidden` = "true"),
        div(
          `aria-live` = "polite",
          uiOutput("national_understanding") %>% withSpinner()
        )
      )
    )
    # NOTE: the "Download Selected Topic" button previously lived here at the
    # foot of the page. It now sits in the controls card, to the right of the
    # category and topic selectors.
  )
  ,
  # Disclosure behaviour for the collapsible topic picker. Delegated listeners
  # on the static #national-topic-region survive the server re-rendering the
  # list on a category change. Selection itself is native (real radios) and
  # reported by Shiny's radio binding; this only opens/closes the panel and
  # manages focus. If the script never runs, the list just stays visible.
  tags$script(HTML("
  (function () {
    var toggle = document.getElementById('national-topic-toggle');
    var region = document.getElementById('national-topic-region');
    if (!toggle || !region) return;
    var field = toggle.parentNode;
    // Timestamp of the last close that was triggered by picking a topic row.
    // Used to swallow a toggle click that lands a beat later (see below).
    var lastRowClose = 0;
    // Viewport scroll captured the instant a topic row is pressed with a mouse
    // or finger, BEFORE the browser moves focus. Restored after the pick so the
    // page does not creep (see the pointerdown / click handlers below). Null for
    // keyboard selection, which keeps its native scroll-focus-into-view.
    var rowScroll = null;
    function isOpen() { return !region.classList.contains('is-collapsed'); }
    // focus() with preventScroll: the real radios are 1px, opacity:0,
    // position:absolute nodes sitting low in a 320px scroll list, so a plain
    // focus() lets the browser scrollIntoView() and yank the page down past the
    // map to the table. preventScroll keeps the caret move invisible.
    function focusNoScroll(el) {
      if (!el) return;
      try { el.focus({ preventScroll: true }); } catch (e) { el.focus(); }
    }
    function openList() {
      region.classList.remove('is-collapsed');
      toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
      focusNoScroll(region.querySelector('input.ntt-radio:checked') ||
                    region.querySelector('input.ntt-radio'));
    }
    function closeList(focusToggle) {
      region.classList.add('is-collapsed');
      toggle.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
      if (focusToggle) focusNoScroll(toggle);
    }
    toggle.addEventListener('click', function () {
      // Picking a topic row auto-closes the list on a 0ms timeout. If the user
      // is also reaching for the collapse caret, their click can land just after
      // that auto-close: without this guard it reads as 'open' and re-expands
      // the list (and refocuses the freshly-checked radio). Treat a toggle click
      // within 400ms of a row-driven close as a no-op.
      if (!isOpen() && (Date.now() - lastRowClose) < 400) return;
      isOpen() ? closeList(true) : openList();
    });
    toggle.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
      // Enter / Space already trigger the button's own click (handled above);
      // wiring them here too raced open-then-closed. Only ArrowDown needs help.
      if (!isOpen() && e.key === 'ArrowDown') { e.preventDefault(); openList(); }
    });
    // Snapshot the scroll position before the click focuses the visually hidden
    // radio. pointerdown fires ahead of the focus move (mouse and touch); a
    // keyboard pick has no pointerdown, so rowScroll stays null there.
    region.addEventListener('pointerdown', function (e) {
      rowScroll = e.target.closest('.ntt-row')
        ? { x: window.scrollX, y: window.scrollY }
        : null;
    });
    region.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
      var s = rowScroll;          // consume the snapshot on any click in the list
      rowScroll = null;
      if (!e.target.closest('.ntt-row')) return;
      lastRowClose = Date.now();
      // Clicking the <label> makes the browser scroll its 1px, off-screen radio
      // into view. For a mouse/touch pick, pin the viewport where the user left
      // it: sync (undo the focus scroll), next frame (spinner reflow settling),
      // and after the 0ms collapse. The toggle above the list never moves, so a
      // restore to the captured offset reads as 'nothing moved'.
      var restore = function () { if (s) window.scrollTo(s.x, s.y); };
      restore();
      requestAnimationFrame(restore);
      setTimeout(function () { closeList(true); restore(); }, 0);
    });
    region.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
      if (e.key === 'Escape' || e.key === 'Enter') { e.preventDefault(); closeList(true); }
    });
    field.addEventListener('focusout', function (e) {
      if (isOpen() && e.relatedTarget && !field.contains(e.relatedTarget)) closeList(false);
    });
    document.addEventListener('mousedown', function (e) {
      if (isOpen() && !field.contains(e.target)) closeList(false);
    });
  })();
  "))
  , adaparc_footer
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Flag to control rendering
  ready_to_render <- reactiveVal(FALSE)

  national_category_selected <- reactive({
    switch(
      input$national_category_selector %||% "Demographics",
      "Demographics"            = "is_demographics",
      "Community Participation" = "is_community_participation",
      "Community Living"        = "is_community_living",
      "Work/Economic"           = "is_work_economic"
    )
  })

  national_variable_choices <- reactive({
    tibble::deframe(
      dict_vars %>%
        filter(
          !!sym(national_category_selected()) == TRUE,
          !is.na(national_dropdown_label)
        ) %>%
        select(national_dropdown_label, var_readable)
    )
  })

  # ── Collapsible topic picker ──────────────────────────────────────────
  # The grouped radio list is server-rendered and re-rendered only when the
  # CATEGORY changes, never on a topic click, so picking a topic never rebuilds
  # the DOM (native radios carry it, Shiny's radio binding reports it). On a
  # category change the new list mounts with its default topic checked, the
  # binding re-reads it and input$national_variable_selector updates.
  # suspendWhenHidden = FALSE so the list renders (and binds) while the picker
  # is collapsed on first paint.
  output$national_topic_group <- renderUI({
    cat_col <- national_category_selected()
    nat_topic_radios(cat_col, nat_topic_default(cat_col))
  })
  outputOptions(output, "national_topic_group", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

  # Label on the collapsed picker button: "Group · Leaf" (or the bare label when
  # it has no group), matching the list rows.
  output$national_topic_current <- renderText({
    req(national_variable_selected())
    lbl <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label)
    if (length(lbl) && grepl(":", lbl, fixed = TRUE)) {
      paste0(trimws(sub(":.*$", "", lbl)), " · ",
             trimws(sub("^[^:]*:\\s*", "", lbl)))
    } else {
      lbl
    }
  })
  outputOptions(output, "national_topic_current", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

  # When both selectors have values, allow rendering
  observe({
    if (!is.null(input$national_category_selector) &&
        !is.null(input$national_variable_selector) &&
        nzchar(input$national_variable_selector)) {
      ready_to_render(TRUE)
    }
  })

  national_variable_selected <- reactive({
    req(national_category_selected())
    choices <- national_variable_choices()
    # If the select has not yet echoed its updated value back to the server,
    # fall back to the default so the table/map still render on first paint.
    current <- input$national_variable_selector
    if (is.null(current) || !nzchar(current) || !(current %in% names(choices))) {
      current <- if ("People with Disabilities" %in% names(choices)) {
        "People with Disabilities"
      } else {
        names(choices)[1]
      }
    }
    req(current)
    choices[[current]]
  })

  # Screen-reader status line for the selection controls (rendered into the
  # visually hidden aria-live region beside the selectors). Announces the
  # active category, how many topics it offers, and which topic is now shown.
  # Wording is kept distinct from output$national_map_summary so the two
  # aria-live regions don't talk over each other.
  output$national_selection_status <- renderText({
    req(national_variable_selected())
    n_topics  <- length(national_variable_choices())
    topic_lbl <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label)
    topic_lbl <- trimws(sub(".*:", "", topic_lbl))
    sprintf(
      "%s category selected. %d topic%s available. Now showing %s.",
      input$national_category_selector %||% "Demographics",
      n_topics,
      if (n_topics == 1) "" else "s",
      topic_lbl
    )
  })
  # The status text lives in a clipped (1x1) container, so keep it rendering
  # even if Shiny's visibility heuristic ever decides otherwise.
  outputOptions(output, "national_selection_status", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

  # Reactively update the map image's aria-label whenever the topic changes,
  # so screen readers announce which variable is currently shown on the map.
  #
  # AUDITED FOR THE STARTUP MESSAGE RACE. Phase 1.4 of
  # docs/palette-v2-build-plan.qmd, 2026-08-03. This observe() fires on the
  # session's first flush, so it sends during startup exactly as the display
  # panel's push did. It is NOT exposed to the same defect, for two independent
  # reasons, and both are properties of where the handler lives rather than
  # luck:
  #
  #   1. The handler is a tags$script in this app's own UI, a few lines below.
  #      It is registered while the browser parses the document body, which is
  #      finished before shiny.js opens the websocket, which is in turn before
  #      the server can flush anything back. Nothing can arrive first. The
  #      display panel's handler is in www/cssloaders.html, injected into the
  #      HEAD ahead of Shiny's own dependencies, so it runs at a point where
  #      `window.Shiny` may not exist yet and registration has to be deferred.
  #      That deferral is the race.
  #
  #   2. If a message were dropped anyway, the div carries a static aria-label
  #      in the markup and the next topic change re-sends. The failure would be
  #      a stale but valid label, not an unusable control.
  #
  # These are the only two sendCustomMessage call sites in this file. If a
  # third is added, and its handler is not in the same document's body, give it
  # a client-initiated handshake like display_panel_ready rather than trusting
  # the ordering.
  observe({
    req(national_variable_selected())
    topic_label <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()
    category_label <- input$national_category_selector
    new_label <- paste0(
      "Choropleth map of the United States showing ", topic_label,
      " (", category_label, ") by state.",
      " Use the topic dropdown above to change the variable displayed."
    )
    session$sendCustomMessage("updateMapAriaLabel", list(label = new_label))
  })

  # ── Shared topic bundle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for the on-screen table AND the downloadable full
  # view. Building the friendly table, title, notes, and alt text here (rather
  # than separately in each output) guarantees the download always matches what
  # the user sees. Consumed by output$sortable_table and the download handler.
  national_topic_bundle <- reactive({
    req(ready_to_render())
    sel     <- national_variable_selected()
    req(sel)
    cat_col <- national_category_selected()

    var_row <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == sel) %>%
      head(1)

    title <- var_row %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    # Interpretation note: only for non-demographic, directional indicators.
    # Mirrors output$national_map_note so the download reads identically.
    is_demo <- isTRUE(var_row %>% pull(is_demographics))
    coding  <- var_row %>% pull(var_coding)
    interp_note <- ""
    if (!(is_demo || is.na(coding) || !(coding %in% c("pos", "neg")))) {
      # The colour reading holds for every series on these maps, not only the
      # disability series, so the note stays neutral on disability status.
      lead <- "Darker colors = more opportunity, lighter color = more disparity. "
      direction <- if (coding == "pos") {
        paste0("'", title, "' is a 'positive' indicator, meaning higher values indicate more opportunity.")
      } else {
        paste0("'", title, "' is a 'negative' indicator, meaning higher values indicate less opportunity.")
      }
      interp_note <- paste0(lead, direction)
    }

    # Data source line (consumed by output$national_understanding and the
    # download's "Understanding This Data" block).
    source_text <- var_row %>% pull(data_source_label)
    if (length(source_text) == 0 || is.na(source_text) || !nzchar(trimws(source_text))) {
      source_text <- "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
    }

    # Population / denominator note for the selected topic. Blank for topics
    # that have not been given one yet, in which case the outputs below and the
    # download simply omit the block.
    universe_text <- var_row %>% pull(universe_note)
    if (length(universe_text) == 0 || is.na(universe_text) ||
        !nzchar(trimws(universe_text))) {
      universe_text <- ""
    }

    # Friendly table (mirrors former inline logic in output$sortable_table)
    national_vars_in_topic <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(
        (!!sym(cat_col)) == TRUE,
        var_topic == (dict_vars %>%
                        filter(
                          (!!sym(cat_col)) == TRUE &
                            var_readable == sel
                        ) %>%
                        pull(var_topic)),
        display == TRUE
      ) %>%
      select(var_pretty, var_readable)

    # Plain-language definition of each column, in table order. Keyed by
    # var_readable, labelled by the same pretty header the table uses. Columns
    # without a definition yet (e.g. the count columns) are dropped, so a topic
    # with no definitions at all yields a zero-row frame and no block renders.
    column_defs <- national_vars_in_topic %>%
      left_join(
        dict_vars %>%
          select(var_readable, pct_definition) %>%
          distinct(var_readable, .keep_all = TRUE),
        by = "var_readable"
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(pct_definition) & nzchar(trimws(pct_definition))) %>%
      transmute(term = var_pretty, definition = trimws(pct_definition))

    table_df <- national_data %>%
      mutate("State" = NAME) %>%
      arrange(State != "United States", State) %>%
      select(any_of(c("State", national_vars_in_topic %>% pull(var_readable)))) %>%
      mutate(
        across(
          c(starts_with("pct_"), ends_with("_pct")),
          ~ scales::percent(.x, accuracy = 0.1, scale = 1)
        ),
        across(
          where(is.numeric) & !starts_with("pct_") & !ends_with("_pct"),
          ~ scales::comma(.x, accuracy = 1)
        )
      ) %>%
      rename(!!!national_vars_in_topic %>% deframe())

    list(
      sel          = sel,
      title        = title,
      category     = input$national_category_selector %||% "",
      interp_note  = interp_note,
      source_note  = source_text,
      universe_note = universe_text,
      column_defs  = column_defs,
      alt_text     = altText(national_data, sel),
      table_df     = table_df,
      vars         = national_vars_in_topic
    )
  })

  output$national_map_summary <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    HTML(
      sprintf(
        '<span class="map-summary">%s</span>',
        altText(national_data, national_variable_selected())
      )
    )
  })

  # "Understanding This Data" card body. One output so the three blocks refresh
  # together and stay in lockstep with the downloaded report (national_topic.qmd
  # builds the same structure from the same bundle fields). "Data source" is
  # always present, so the card always renders; the other two blocks appear only
  # when the selected topic has been given that text in dict_vars.
  output$national_understanding <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    b <- national_topic_bundle()

    # Decorative glyph inside a solid navy chip; aria-hidden. Kept as literal
    # SVG so the same markup can be reused verbatim in the download template.
    chip <- function(kind) {
      p <- switch(
        kind,
        pop = '<circle cx="9" cy="8" r="3.1"/><path d="M3.7 19c0-2.9 2.4-4.8 5.3-4.8S14.3 16.1 14.3 19"/><circle cx="16.8" cy="9.6" r="2.5"/><path d="M15 14.3c2.3.2 4.3 1.9 4.3 4.7"/>',
        src = '<path d="M6 3.6h7.5L18 8.1V19.4a1 1 0 0 1-1 1H6a1 1 0 0 1-1-1V4.6a1 1 0 0 1 1-1z"/><path d="M13.3 3.6v4.6H18"/><path d="M8.4 12.4h7M8.4 15.8h7"/>',
        pct = '<path d="M6.5 17.5 17.5 6.5"/><circle cx="8.3" cy="8.3" r="2.1"/><circle cx="15.7" cy="15.7" r="2.1"/>'
      )
      HTML(sprintf(
        paste0('<span class="understanding-chip" aria-hidden="true">',
               '<svg class="understanding-glyph" viewBox="0 0 24 24" focusable="false">%s</svg>',
               '</span>'),
        p
      ))
    }

    blocks <- list()

    note <- b$universe_note %||% ""
    if (nzchar(trimws(note))) {
      blocks <- c(blocks, list(div(
        class = "understanding-block",
        h3(class = "understanding-subhead", chip("pop"), "Population Examined"),
        p(class = "understanding-body", note)
      )))
    }

    src <- b$source_note %||% ""
    if (!nzchar(trimws(src))) {
      src <- "2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates"
    }
    blocks <- c(blocks, list(div(
      class = "understanding-block",
      h3(class = "understanding-subhead", chip("src"), "Data Source"),
      p(class = "understanding-body", src)
    )))

    defs <- b$column_defs
    if (is.data.frame(defs) && nrow(defs) > 0) {
      blocks <- c(blocks, list(div(
        class = "understanding-block",
        h3(class = "understanding-subhead", chip("pct"),
           "What Each Percentage Column Means"),
        tags$dl(
          class = "understanding-defs",
          lapply(seq_len(nrow(defs)), function(i) {
            tags$div(
              class = "understanding-def",
              tags$dt(defs$term[i]),
              tags$dd(defs$definition[i])
            )
          })
        ),
        p(class = "understanding-defs-note",
          "Count columns (#) show the number of people each percentage is based on.")
      )))
    }

    tagList(div(class = "understanding-sections", blocks))
  })

  output$national_map_title <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    title <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()
    div(h2(title, class = "national-map-title"))
  })

  output$national_table_title <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    title <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1) %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    div(h2(title, class = "national-map-title"))
  })

  # Interpretation note shown in its own container ABOVE the map. The note
  # only applies to non-demographic indicators with an explicit pos/neg
  # direction. Coloring is now directional (dark = better outcome), so the
  # note explains that convention and names the indicator's direction.
  output$national_map_note <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())

    var_row <- dict_vars %>%
      filter(var_readable == national_variable_selected()) %>%
      head(1)

    is_demo <- isTRUE(var_row %>% pull(is_demographics))
    coding  <- var_row %>% pull(var_coding)

    title <- var_row %>%
      pull(national_dropdown_label) %>%
      sub(".*:", "", .) %>%
      trimws()

    if (is_demo || is.na(coding) || !(coding %in% c("pos", "neg"))) {
      return(NULL)
    }

    # Kept identical to the download copy above: the colour reading applies to
    # every series on the map, regardless of disability status.
    lead <- "Darker colors = more opportunity, lighter color = more disparity. "
    direction <- if (coding == "pos") {
      paste0("'", title, "' is a 'positive' indicator, meaning higher values indicate more opportunity.")
    } else {
      paste0("'", title, "' is a 'negative' indicator, meaning higher values indicate less opportunity.")
    }

    div(
      class = "map-interpretation-note",
      tags$span(class = "map-interpretation-note-label", "Interpretation Note: "),
      paste0(lead, direction)
    )
  })

  output$national_ggmap <- renderGirafe({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    gg <- render_national_map(
      national_variable_selected(),
      access_map_palette_selected(),
      na_color = access_map_na_selected()
    )
    girafe(
      ggobj      = gg,
      # 10 x 6 rather than 10 x 5. The legend sits at the bottom in two rows,
      # so the map panel was about 10 x 3.8, far wider than the Albers US
      # outline needs; the map was height-constrained and left large empty
      # flanks either side. A taller canvas gives the panel back to the map
      # instead of the margins. Legend and tooltip type do not change size,
      # since the SVG is scaled to the container width, not its height.
      width_svg  = 10,
      height_svg = 6,
      options    = list(
        opts_tooltip(
          css = paste0(
            "background:#1c2b3a; color:white; ",
            "font-family:'EB Garamond',Georgia,serif; ",
            "font-size:15px; padding:8px 11px; border-radius:6px; ",
            "line-height:1.55; white-space:pre;"
          ),
          offx = 12, offy = -28, use_cursor_pos = TRUE
        ),
        # Deliberately sets stroke-WIDTH only, never stroke colour. Each state
        # now carries a border colour chosen from its own fill (near-black on
        # the light half of the ramp, white on the dark half; see the State
        # border ink notes in scripts/functions.R). Forcing a single navy on
        # hover, as this did before, overwrote that and left dark-filled states
        # with a 1.3:1 hover outline they could not show. Widening the state's
        # own ink keeps the hover affordance legible on every bin and in every
        # palette.
        opts_hover(css = "fill-opacity:0.75; stroke-width:2px;"),
        opts_sizing(rescale = TRUE, width = 1),
        opts_toolbar(saveaspng = FALSE),
        opts_selection(type = "none")
      )
    )
  })

  output$national_table <- renderUI({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
    DT::dataTableOutput("sortable_table", width = "100%")
  })

  output$sortable_table <- DT::renderDataTable({
    req(ready_to_render())
    req(national_variable_selected())
```
