```{r National Data}
    # Table content comes from the shared bundle so it always matches the
    # downloadable full view (see national_topic_bundle above).
    bundle <- national_topic_bundle()
    national_data_table_friendly <- bundle$table_df

    all_columns      <- colnames(national_data_table_friendly)
    sortable_columns <- which(grepl("State|%", all_columns))

    # DataTables uses 0-based column indices; 0 is the State column
    non_state_columns <- setdiff(seq_along(all_columns) - 1, 0)

    # Per-table CSV export removed: downloading is now handled by the single
    # "Download Selected Topic" full-view button at the bottom of the page.
    DT::datatable(
      national_data_table_friendly,
      options = list(
        pageLength = -1,  # show all rows by default
        lengthMenu = list(
          c(10, 25, 50, -1),
          c("10", "25", "50", "All")
        ),
        scrollX   = TRUE,
        autoWidth = FALSE,
        columnDefs = list(
          # Make some columns unsortable
          list(
            targets   = setdiff(seq_along(all_columns) - 1, sortable_columns - 1),
            orderable = FALSE
          ),
          # Right-align all non-State columns
          list(
            targets   = non_state_columns,
            className = 'dt-right'
          )
        ),
        dom     = "lfrtip"  # length, filter, table, info, paging (no Buttons)
      ),
      rownames = FALSE,
      width    = "100%",
      # "compact" dropped: its 4px cell padding fought the roomier row
      # heights set in the national table CSS above.
      class    = "display table_national"
    )
  }, server = FALSE)

  # ── Download Selected Topic: full branded HTML view ─────────────────────────
  # Renders national_topic.qmd for the current selection into a self-contained,
  # ADA-PARC branded HTML: page 1 (banner, title, map + key, notes), page 2
  # (data table). All content is prepared here and passed via an RDS bundle so
  # the download always matches the on-screen view.
  nd_app_root <- normalizePath(
    getOption("shiny.appdir", default = getwd()),
    mustWork = FALSE
  )
  national_dir  <- file.path(nd_app_root, "national")
  national_qmd  <- file.path(national_dir, "national_topic.qmd")
  nd_out_dir    <- file.path(tempdir(), "ada_parc_national_dl")
  dir.create(nd_out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  output$download_national_topic <- downloadHandler(
    filename = function() {
      bundle <- national_topic_bundle()
      slug   <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", bundle$title)
      slug   <- gsub("^_|_$", "", slug)
      paste0("ADA-PARC_", slug, "_2024.html")
    },
    content = function(file) {
      withProgress(
        message = "Building your ADA-PARC report…",
        detail  = "This usually takes 15–25 seconds.",
        value   = 0.2,
        {
          bundle <- national_topic_bundle()

          # Render the map (ggplot from render_national_map) to an inline SVG
          # string. svglite emits the requested font-family; the browser pairs
          # it with the EB Garamond webfont loaded via font-loader.html.
          gg <- render_national_map(
            bundle$sel,
            access_map_palette_selected(),
            na_color = access_map_na_selected()
          )
          svg_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".svg")
          ggplot2::ggsave(
            filename = svg_tmp, plot = gg,
            device = svglite::svglite,
            width = 9, height = 6.4, bg = "white"
          )
          map_svg <- paste(readLines(svg_tmp, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
          unlink(svg_tmp)

          setProgress(0.45, detail = "Composing the document…")

          out_bundle <- list(
            title       = bundle$title,
            category    = bundle$category,
            interp_note = bundle$interp_note,
            source_note = bundle$source_note,
            universe_note = bundle$universe_note,
            column_defs = bundle$column_defs,
            alt_text    = bundle$alt_text,
            table_df    = bundle$table_df,
            map_svg     = map_svg,
            generated   = format(Sys.Date(), "%B %d, %Y")
          )
          bundle_path <- file.path(nd_out_dir, "bundle.rds")
          saveRDS(out_bundle, bundle_path)

          setProgress(0.6, detail = "Rendering HTML…")

          tryCatch({
            quarto::quarto_render(
              input          = national_qmd,
              execute_params = list(bundle = bundle_path),
              execute_dir    = national_dir
            )
            rendered <- file.path(national_dir, "national_topic.html")
            if (file.exists(rendered)) {
              fix_decorative_banner_alt(rendered)  # audit finding C3
              file.copy(rendered, file, overwrite = TRUE)
            } else {
              writeLines("<html><body>Report could not be generated.</body></html>", file)
            }
            setProgress(1)
          }, error = function(e) {
            showNotification(
              ui       = paste("Download failed:", conditionMessage(e)),
              type     = "error",
              duration = 15
            )
            writeLines(
              paste0("<html><body>Report could not be generated: ",
                     htmltools::htmlEscape(conditionMessage(e)), "</body></html>"),
              file
            )
          })
        }
      )
    }
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

# City Data

```{r}
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(leaflet.extras2)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(scales)
library(shinycssloaders)

# ----------------------------
# State choices
# ----------------------------
state_choices <- tibble::tibble(NAME = state.name, ABB = state.abb) %>%
  add_row(NAME = c("District of Columbia", "Puerto Rico"), ABB = c("DC", "PR")) %>%
  tibble::deframe()

# Grouped choices for the native <select> (selectize = FALSE): 50 states + D.C.
# A–Z, then a one-item Territories optgroup. Option VALUES stay the display
# names — the server still maps name -> abbreviation through state_choices.
# The optgroup gives screen readers a spoken section boundary and keeps Puerto
# Rico from looking like a missing state at the bottom of the list.
state_select_choices <- list(
  `States & D.C.` = as.list(sort(c(state.name, "District of Columbia"))),
  `Territories`   = list("Puerto Rico")
)

# Cities for the default state (Illinois), so the #city_selector <select> paints
# populated on first load rather than briefly empty before the state observer
# flushes. Same filter/order as the city_choices() reactive.
initial_city_choices <- dict_location_crosswalk %>%
  dplyr::filter(state == "IL", !stringr::str_detect(place_NAME, " CDP")) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(place_NAME) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(place_NAME) %>%
  dplyr::pull(place_NAME)

# ----------------------------
# Helpers (ALL pct cols are dbl on 0–100 scale)
# ----------------------------
fmt_pct_1dp <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.1))
}

# As above, but adds precision as the value shrinks: one decimal at 1% and
# above, two decimals under 1%, three decimals under 0.01%. One decimal
# alone rounds small shares to 0.0% and loses them; two decimals still
# rounds the smallest shares (well under 0.01%) to 0.00%. Used on the
# Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age demographics list, where "share of total
# population" figures routinely fall under 1%.
fmt_pct_dynamic <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA",
         ifelse(abs(x) < 0.01,
                scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.001),
                ifelse(abs(x) < 1,
                       scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.01),
                       scales::percent(x / 100, accuracy = 0.1))))
}

fmt_num <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "NA", scales::comma(x, accuracy = 1))
}

create_number_percent_string <- function(num, pct) {
  paste0(fmt_num(num), " (", fmt_pct_1dp(pct), ")")
}

# Dollar formatter for ACS median earnings (B18140).
#
# ACS reports a median that falls in the top or bottom interval as the
# bound itself, so the raw values 250001 and 2499 are not real medians and
# must not be printed as though they were. Across the 8,407 places, 6 are
# top-coded and 40 are bottom-coded.
fmt_dollar <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(x)    ~ "Not available",
    x >= 250001 ~ "$250,000 or more",
    x <= 2499   ~ "$2,500 or less",
    TRUE        ~ scales::dollar(x, accuracy = 1)
  )
}

# As above, but collapses to a plain-language phrase when the percentage is
# suppressed, so the reader sees "Not available" rather than "NA (NA)".
# Used for indicators that are genuinely missing for some places: health
# insurance (a handful of places) and anything sourced from ACS S1811,
# which resolves for only 694 of 8,407 places.
create_number_percent_string_or_na <- function(num, pct) {
  ifelse(is.na(as.numeric(pct)), "Not available",
         paste0(fmt_num(num), " (", fmt_pct_1dp(pct), ")"))
}

# As fmt_pct_1dp, but "Not available" rather than "NA" for a missing value.
# Used where there is no paired count to fall back on the way
# create_number_percent_string_or_na does: HUD housing access is a rate
# with no numerator/denominator pair carried on this page.
fmt_pct_or_na <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "Not available", fmt_pct_1dp(x))
}

# One decimal place, "mi" suffix, "Not available" for a missing value. Used
# for the Centers for Independent Living distance measures, which are place-
# level straight-line distances rather than a rate with a numerator/
# denominator pair.
fmt_miles_or_na <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  ifelse(is.na(x), "Not available", paste0(scales::comma(x, accuracy = 0.1), " mi"))
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paired with/without-disability comparison tables (City Data tab)
#
# Every outcome indicator on the city page has a without-disability
# counterpart in city_place_full.Rds, at equal or better coverage. These two
# helpers render a pair as an accessible two-column table rather than as a
# bullet list, because a bullet carrying two values reads as a run-on
# sentence and gives screen reader users no column context.
#
# The PWD-to-PWOD column pairs MUST be declared explicitly. The naming is not
# consistent and cannot be derived: unemployment is
# pct_cni_18to64_nodis_unemployed, with "nodis" before the measure, while its
# neighbour is pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis with "nodis" after, and the
# health insurance columns put "nodis" in the middle. A
# paste0(var, "_nodis") would fail silently on several of them.
#
# cmp_row() builds one row spec. kind = "count_pct" formats as
# "12,345 (12.3%)"; kind = "dollar" formats a single ACS median with the
# top-code and bottom-code guards in fmt_dollar().
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cmp_row <- function(label, dis, nodis, kind = "count_pct", dis_pop = NA_character_,
                    nodis_pop = NA_character_) {
  list(label = label, dis = dis, nodis = nodis, kind = kind,
       dis_pop = dis_pop, nodis_pop = nodis_pop)
}

render_comparison_table <- function(row, rows, caption) {
  cell <- function(pct_col, pop_col, kind) {
    if (identical(kind, "dollar")) {
      fmt_dollar(row[[pct_col]])
    } else {
      create_number_percent_string_or_na(row[[pop_col]], row[[pct_col]])
    }
  }

  body <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    paste0(
      "<tr><th scope=\"row\">", r$label, "</th>",
      "<td>", cell(r$dis,   r$dis_pop,   r$kind), "</td>",
      "<td>", cell(r$nodis, r$nodis_pop, r$kind), "</td></tr>"
    )
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<table class=\"city-compare\">",
    "<caption>", caption, "</caption>",
    "<thead><tr>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">Indicator</th>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">With disability</th>",
    "<th scope=\"col\">Without disability</th>",
    "</tr></thead><tbody>",
    paste0(body, collapse = ""),
    "</tbody></table>"
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Disability Demographics list (Race/Ethnicity, Sex, Age) on the City Data tab
#
# Simplified per Colin's client's request 2026-08-18: these three groups
# used to render as four-column tables (see git history / render_share_table()
# for the prior version), answering three separate questions per group
# (disability rate within the group, share of the city's PWD, share of the
# total population). The client asked to drop back to a single, plainly
# readable figure per group:
#   - the number of people in that group with a disability
#     -> pop_cni_<group>_dis
#   - that number's share of the city's total population
#     -> pop_cni_<group>_dis / pop_cni_total_all
#     ("Of everyone in this city, what share is both disabled and X?")
#
# Both are derivable from columns already present in city_place(): the
# disabled headcount per group (pop_cni_<group>_dis) and the city's total
# population (pop_cni_total_all). No new pipeline variables are needed.
# Renders as a plain <ul>, not a table, per the client's request for a
# cleaner, simpler look; a native list still gives screen reader users list
# structure without table markup the two figures no longer need.
#
# Layout, 2026-08-18 second follow-up: each group is a stat tile rather than
# a single label/value line, and the <ul> is a responsive CSS grid, so the
# groups fill the full-width card instead of stacking in one narrow column
# that left most of the card empty. Inside a tile the reading order is
# label (a bold term and, where the label carried a "(gloss)", a lighter
# description line), then a .city-demo-figs row holding the share of total
# population set large as the headline figure and the count beside it, split
# by a hairline (Colin 2026-09-08; the count sat beneath until then). Sizing
# and colour live in the stylesheet (.city-demo-list and friends); this
# function only emits markup.
#
# Accessibility notes on the tile markup:
#   - the <ul>/<li> structure is unchanged, so screen readers still announce
#     the group count and step through one group at a time;
#   - the headline percentage is visually labelled only by its position, so
#     a visually hidden span (.city-demo-sr) carries the words a sighted
#     reader gets from the heading above and the count beside it. Without it
#     the percentage would be read as a bare number;
#   - the count carries a visible "residents" unit rather than a bare
#     number, and nothing is encoded in colour or by a bar.
#
# The whole figure block is built in one is.na() branch rather than
# concatenated from separately-computed pieces, so a missing group_dis
# collapses cleanly to a single "Not available" tile rather than pairing a
# real "Not available" with a leftover formatted "NA".
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
demo_row <- function(label, group_dis_pop) {
  list(label = label, group_dis_pop = group_dis_pop)
}

# One tile. Split out of render_demo_list() on 2026-08-18 so the Disability
# Types block can emit the same markup without duplicating the class names
# in a second place. figure is already-built HTML; label is a plain string
# that demo_label_html() splits into a bold term and, where the label
# carried a "(plain-language gloss)", a lighter description line beneath it.
demo_tile <- function(label, figure) {
  paste0(
    "<li class=\"city-demo-tile\">",
    demo_label_html(label),
    figure,
    "</li>"
  )
}

# "Ambulatory (difficulty walking or climbing stairs)" -> a "city-demo-term"
# span for "Ambulatory" and a "city-demo-desc" span for the gloss, shown on
# its own line (roman, not italic, per Colin 2026-09-08). Labels with no
# trailing "(...)" -- every race, sex and age band -- get the term span only.
# "Some other race(s) identified" does not match: the pattern needs the "("
# preceded by a space and the ")" at the very end of the string.
# The gloss keeps its own line rather than parentheses so the term reads as
# a field name, and a screen reader gets "term  gloss" with no bracket
# characters spoken.
demo_label_html <- function(label) {
  parts <- regmatches(label, regexec("^\\s*(.+?)\\s+\\((.+)\\)\\s*$", label))[[1]]
  term  <- if (length(parts) == 3L) parts[2] else label
  desc  <- if (length(parts) == 3L) parts[3] else NA_character_
  paste0(
    "<span class=\"city-demo-label\">",
    "<span class=\"city-demo-term\">", term, "</span>",
    if (is.na(desc)) "" else paste0("<span class=\"city-demo-desc\">", desc, "</span>"),
    "</span>"
  )
}

# The figure half of a tile: the headline percentage and the count sit side
# by side in a .city-demo-figs row, split by a hairline rule, with the
# percentage keeping the visual lead. Both the demographics groups and the
# disability types express the same quantity, a share of the city's total
# population, so both carry the same visually hidden wording -- which is now
# the only thing telling a screen reader what the bare percentage means, so
# it stays even though the visible layout no longer spells it out. Built in
# one branch rather than concatenated from separately-computed pieces, so a
# missing value collapses to a single "Not available" rather than pairing a
# real "Not available" with a leftover formatted "NA".
demo_figure <- function(pct, count) {
  pct   <- as.numeric(pct)
  count <- as.numeric(count)
  if (is.na(pct)) {
    return("<span class=\"city-demo-figs\"><span class=\"city-demo-na\">Not available</span></span>")
  }
  paste0(
    "<span class=\"city-demo-figs\">",
    "<span class=\"city-demo-pct\">",
    fmt_pct_dynamic(pct),
    "<span class=\"city-demo-sr\"> of the city's total population</span>",
    "</span>",
    if (is.na(count)) {
      ""
    } else {
      paste0(
        "<span class=\"city-demo-count\">",
        "<span class=\"city-demo-count-val\">", fmt_num(count), "</span>",
        "<span class=\"city-demo-count-unit\"> residents</span>",
        "</span>"
      )
    },
    "</span>"
  )
}

# note is optional explanatory prose shown between the heading and the tiles.
# Added 2026-08-18 for the Age block, whose under-5 caveat previously sat
# above the "Age" heading, where it read as though it applied to Sex. It
# carries .city-summary-help, the on-screen note class, which the download
# template also styles (see .tbl-block p.city-summary-help in
# city/city_profile.qmd), so the one fragment reads correctly in both.
render_demo_list <- function(row, rows, heading, note = NULL) {
  total_pop <- as.numeric(row$pop_cni_total_all)

  items <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    group_dis <- as.numeric(row[[r$group_dis_pop]])
    pct <- if (is.na(group_dis) || is.na(total_pop) || total_pop == 0) {
      NA_real_
    } else {
      100 * group_dis / total_pop
    }
    demo_tile(r$label, demo_figure(pct, group_dis))
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<p class=\"city-demo-heading\">", heading, "</p>",
    if (is.null(note) || !nzchar(note)) {
      ""
    } else {
      paste0("<p class=\"city-summary-help\">", note, "</p>")
    },
    "<ul class=\"city-demo-list\">",
    paste0(items, collapse = ""),
    "</ul>"
  )
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Disability Types tiles
#
# Same tile aesthetic as the demographics lists, per Colin's 2026-08-18
# request. Previously a plain <ul> of "Hearing - 12,345 (2.3%)" bullets.
#
# The percentages here come straight from the pipeline's pct_cni_* columns
# rather than being derived from a count and a denominator, because these
# are already shares of the city's total population (see
# help$disability_types_intro), which is exactly what the demographics
# tiles show. So the two blocks are directly comparable and the same
# visually hidden wording inside .city-demo-pct is correct for both.
#
# No wrapping <ul> is added by the caller: this returns the complete list,
# unlike the earlier bullets fragment.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
type_row <- function(label, count_col, pct_col) {
  list(label = label, count_col = count_col, pct_col = pct_col)
}

render_type_list <- function(row, rows) {
  items <- vapply(rows, function(r) {
    demo_tile(r$label, demo_figure(row[[r$pct_col]], row[[r$count_col]]))
  }, character(1))

  paste0(
    "<ul class=\"city-demo-list\">",
    paste0(items, collapse = ""),
    "</ul>"
  )
}

# Join-proof tract GEOID normalization (NO percent conversion)
normalize_tract_geoid <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x)
  x <- gsub("[^0-9]", "", x)                   # digits only
  ifelse(nchar(x) >= 11, substr(x, nchar(x) - 10, nchar(x)), x)  # last 11 digits
}

# ----------------------------
# UI
# ----------------------------
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* ── City Data tab: font + design tokens ──────────────────────────── */
      /* @import here because the shinyApp sub-context does not reliably     */
      /* inherit www/styles.css from the parent flexdashboard.               */
      @import url('https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=EB+Garamond:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;0,800;1,400&display=swap');

      /* Universal font rule — covers Bootstrap resets and dynamic widgets */
      *, *::before, *::after {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
      }

      body {
        background: #f9f7f4;
      }

      /* Page header banner */
      /* Banner geometry, title and intro line are kept byte-for-byte identical
         to .national-banner / .national-banner h1 / .national-intro so the two
         tabs open with the same header block. Values are in px because
         Bootstrap 3 sets html{font-size:10px}, which makes rem units render
         ~62% of their intended size here. */
      .city-banner {
        background: #f9f7f4;
        border-bottom: 3px solid #e8e4db;
        padding: 20px 24px 18px;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        border-radius: 6px 6px 0 0;
      }

      .city-title {
        font-size: 31px;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 6px;
      }
      /* Overrides .city-note (weight 600, 72ch measure, line-height 1.6),
         which applies to the body-copy notes elsewhere on the tab but not to
         this header line. */
      .city-banner .city-note {
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif;
        font-size: 18px;
        font-weight: 400;
        line-height: inherit;
        max-width: none;
        color: #2c2c2c;
        margin-top: 0;
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }
      .city-note {
        font-size: 1.15rem;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.6;
        max-width: 72ch;
        /* Regular weight: this class now only styles the long footer caveat,
           and semibold over ~150 words of running text hurts readability. */
        font-weight: 400;
      }
      /* The footer caveat sits under the full-width two-column summary, so
         the 72ch measure inherited from .city-note made it look as though
         it belonged to the left column only. */
      .city-note-footer {
        max-width: none;
        margin-top: 1rem;
      }

      /* Section cards */
      .city-card {
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e4e8ef;
        border-radius: 8px;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem 1.5rem 1.5rem;
        margin-bottom: 1.25rem;
        box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(28, 43, 58, 0.07);
      }
      .city-controls-card,
      .city-map-card,
      .city-data-summary-card {
        border-top: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
      }

      /* Controls card: label and input text — match national data styling
         (18px / 600, ink). */
      .city-controls-card .shiny-input-container label {
        font-size: 18px;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-weight: 600;
      }

      /* Native <select> (selectize = FALSE): carry over the look the selectize
         box had — 1.5px #5c6672 border, 4px radius, white ground — and give it
         a real ~44px target height. */
      .city-controls-card select.form-control {
        font-size: 18px !important;
        color: #1c2b3a !important;
        min-height: 44px;
        padding: 9px 12px !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #5c6672 !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        background-color: #ffffff !important;
        box-shadow: none !important;
      }
      /* Bootstrap 3's default is a faint blue inset glow with the outline
         suppressed; restore the app-wide 3px focus ring instead. */
      .city-controls-card select.form-control:focus,
      .city-controls-card select.form-control:focus-visible {
        border-color: #0d3b8e !important;
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e !important;
        outline-offset: 2px;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(13, 59, 142, 0.15) !important;
      }

      /* Visually hidden, still announced (clip pattern — not display:none). */
      .city-sr-only {
        position: absolute;
        width: 1px;
        height: 1px;
        padding: 0;
        margin: -1px;
        overflow: hidden;
        clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
        clip-path: inset(50%);
        white-space: nowrap;
        border: 0;
      }

      /* ── Controls row + download action ────────────────────────────────
         Mirrors .national-controls-split / .national-control-action in the
         National Data tab: selectors on the left, the download behind a
         full-height rule on the right, so the two tabs' controls read the
         same way. */
      .city-controls-split {
        display: flex;
        align-items: stretch;
        gap: 1.5rem;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
      }
      .city-controls-row {
        flex: 1 1 auto;
        min-width: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-wrap: wrap;
        align-items: flex-start;
        gap: 1.25rem;
      }
      .city-control-field {
        flex: 1 1 16rem;
        min-width: 0;
      }
      .city-control-field .form-group {
        margin-bottom: 0;
      }
      .city-control-action {
        flex: 0 0 auto;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        justify-content: center;
        border-left: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
        padding-left: 1.5rem;
      }
      /* Download button: kept byte-for-byte in step with .btn-download-national
         so the two tabs' primary action reads the same — 48px target,
         12px/30px padding, 7px radius, 18px/600 centred label on one line.
         Sized in px because this fluidPage() resolves rem against a 10px
         Bootstrap-3 root. */
      .btn-download-city {
        display: inline-flex !important;
        align-items: center !important;
        justify-content: center !important;
        min-height: 48px !important;
        padding: 12px 30px !important;
        background: #013176 !important;
        color: #ffffff !important;
        border: 1.5px solid #013176 !important;
        border-radius: 7px !important;
        font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important;
        font-size: 18px !important;
        font-weight: 600 !important;
        line-height: 1.2 !important;
        letter-spacing: 0.01em !important;
        white-space: nowrap !important;
        text-align: center !important;
        cursor: pointer !important;
        transition: background-color .12s ease, border-color .12s ease !important;
      }
      .btn-download-city:hover {
        background: #01214f !important;
        border-color: #01214f !important;
      }
      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
        .btn-download-city { transition: none !important; }
      }
      /* Button fill is #013176 navy and the #0d3b8e focus token is nearly the
         same blue, so the ring sinks into it. Use the dark ink ring (~14:1 on
         white) with a 3px white halo so focus is unmistakable. */
      .btn-download-city:focus,
      .btn-download-city:focus-visible {
        outline: 3px solid #1c2b3a !important;
        outline-offset: 3px !important;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px #ffffff !important;
      }
      .btn-download-city:disabled,
      .btn-download-city[disabled] {
        opacity: 0.5 !important;
        cursor: not-allowed !important;
      }
      @media (max-width: 900px) {
        .city-controls-split { flex-wrap: wrap; }
        .city-control-action {
          flex: 1 1 100%;
          justify-content: flex-start;
          border-left: none;
          border-top: 1px solid #d8cdb8;
          padding-left: 0;
          padding-top: 1rem;
        }
        .city-control-field .form-group { margin-bottom: 0.25rem; }
      }

      /* City map title */
      .city-map-title {
        color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 2rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-bottom: 0.6rem;
        margin-top: 0.6rem;
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      }

      /* Summary card: warm white background, maroon accent borders */
      .city-summary {
        color: #1c1c1c;
        margin: 1.25rem 0 1.5rem 0;
        padding: 1.25rem 1.5rem 1.5rem 1.5rem;
        background: #ffffff;
        border: 1px solid #e0dbd2;
        border-top: 5px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 5px;
        height: 100%;
        box-sizing: border-box;
        box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.06);
      }
      .city-summary h3,
      .city-summary h4,
      .city-summary p,
      .city-summary ul,
      .city-summary li,
      .city-summary b {
        color: #1c1c1c;
      }
      .city-summary h3 {
        font-size: 2.4rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin: 0.25rem 0 0.9rem 0;
        padding-bottom: 0.45rem;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #1c2b3a;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      }
      .city-summary h4 {
        font-size: 2rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-top: 1.4rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.4rem;
        padding-left: 0.6rem;
        border-left: 3px solid #1c2b3a;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        line-height: 1.3;
      }
      .city-summary p {
        font-size: 1.55rem;
        line-height: 1.75;
        margin-bottom: 0.75rem;
      }
      .city-summary b {
        font-weight: 700;
      }
      /* Sub-headings inside a summary card: Health Insurance, Education,
         Employment, and so on. Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age carry their own
         heading style, .city-demo-heading, styled below near .city-demo-list.
         The two descendant selectors below were written for an older
         markup where the b element sat inside a nested div; in the
         current markup the b element is a direct child of .city-summary,
         so neither matched and sub-headings were rendering at inherited
         body size, smaller than the 1.5rem list items they label. The
         direct-child selector is the one that actually applies. The other
         two are kept in case that markup returns. */
      .city-summary > b,
      .city-summary > div > b,
      .city-summary .col-md-12 > b {
        display: inline-block;
        font-size: 1.55rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin-top: 0.75rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.35rem;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        letter-spacing: 0.01em;
      }
      .city-summary ul {
        font-size: 1.5rem;
        line-height: 1.8;
        margin-top: 0.35rem;
        margin-bottom: 1rem;
        padding-left: 1.5rem;
      }
      .city-summary li {
        margin-bottom: 0.45rem;
        padding-left: 0.1rem;
      }
      .city-summary .city-summary-help {
        font-size: 1.4rem;
        font-style: normal;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        margin-top: -0.1rem;
        margin-bottom: 0.85rem;
        line-height: 1.65;
      }

      /* Paired with/without-disability comparison tables.
         Semantic tables rather than bullet lists: column and row headers are
         announced by screen readers, and tabular figures keep the two value
         columns aligned so the comparison is readable at a glance. */
      .city-summary table.city-compare {
        width: 100%;
        border-collapse: collapse;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1.1rem;
        font-size: 1.4rem;
        line-height: 1.5;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare caption {
        text-align: left;
        font-weight: 700;
        font-size: 1.45rem;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        padding: 0 0 0.3rem;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare th,
      .city-summary table.city-compare td {
        border: 1px solid #ded8cf;
        padding: 0.4rem 0.55rem;
        text-align: left;
        vertical-align: top;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare thead th {
        background: #1c2b3a;
        color: #ffffff;
        font-weight: 600;
        border-color: #1c2b3a;
        font-size: 1.3rem;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] {
        background: #f6f2ec;
        font-weight: 600;
        width: 42%;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare tbody tr:nth-child(even) td {
        background: #fbf9f6;
      }
      .city-summary table.city-compare td {
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
        white-space: nowrap;
      }
      /* Narrow screens: allow the value columns to wrap rather than forcing a
         horizontal scroll inside the card. */
      @media (max-width: 62em) {
        .city-summary table.city-compare td { white-space: normal; }
        .city-summary table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] { width: 38%; }
      }

      /* Full-width outcome cards (Community Participation, Work and
         Economic), stacked one above the other since 2026-08-18 rather than
         sharing a row as col-md-6 halves. With twice the width available,
         the type inside them goes up rather than the tables simply getting
         wider: at half width these tables were set at 1.4rem to fit, which
         is the smallest text on the card and sits below the 1.5rem list
         items beside it. The sizes below bring the tables level with the
         rest of the card and give the cells room to breathe.

         Gated on min-width 62em, Bootstrap 3's md breakpoint and the point
         at which these cards would previously have split into halves.
         Below it the card is full width for every layout anyway and the
         compact sizes above, including the narrow-screen th width in the
         media query directly above this one, still apply. Selectors carry
         both class names so they outrank the base .city-summary rules on
         specificity rather than on source order alone. */
      @media (min-width: 62em) {
        /* max-width, not width, so the table still fills a narrower card.
           On a wide monitor a 100%-width three-column table pushes the two
           value columns so far apart that the eye loses the row it is
           reading; the cap holds the comparison within one comfortable
           glance, the same measure the downloadable report gets from its
           8.5in page. Well above the point where the columns would crowd. */
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare {
          font-size: 1.6rem;
          line-height: 1.55;
          margin: 0.45rem 0 1.4rem;
          max-width: 110rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare caption {
          font-size: 1.7rem;
          padding-bottom: 0.4rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare th,
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare td {
          padding: 0.6rem 0.85rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare thead th {
          font-size: 1.5rem;
        }
        /* The label column no longer needs 42% of a half-width card; at full
           width that would strand the two value columns far to the right of
           the text they belong to. */
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack table.city-compare tbody th[scope='row'] {
          width: 34%;
        }
        /* Sub-headings (Health Insurance, Employment, ...) and their notes,
           raised to keep the same step down from heading to note to table
           that the card had at the smaller sizes. */
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack > b {
          font-size: 1.75rem;
          margin-top: 1.1rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack .city-summary-help {
          font-size: 1.5rem;
        }
        .city-summary.city-summary-stack ul {
          font-size: 1.6rem;
        }
      }

      /* Disability Demographics stat tiles (Race/Ethnicity, Sex, Age).
         Simplified per Colin's client's request 2026-08-18: these three
         groups no longer render as four-column tables (count, rate within
         group, share of city PWD, share of total population). Each group
         now shows two figures, its share of the city's total population as
         the headline and the count beside it, split by a hairline (the
         count sat beneath the percentage from 2026-08-18 until Colin's
         2026-09-08 revision). See render_demo_list().

         Laid out as a responsive grid of tiles, replacing the earlier
         single narrow column. That column was capped at 30rem to keep a
         short label near its value, which fixed the gap but left most of
         this full-width card (.city-summary-wide) empty and made the eight
         race groups read as one undifferentiated stack. auto-fill rather
         than auto-fit is deliberate: with auto-fit a two-item list, Sex,
         would stretch its two tiles across the entire card, so the tile
         size would change from section to section. auto-fill holds the
         track width steady and simply leaves the unused tracks empty.

         Still a native ul/li, so screen readers announce the group count
         and step through one group at a time. The visually hidden span
         inside the percentage (.city-demo-sr) supplies the wording a
         sighted reader takes from the tile layout; without it the headline
         reads as a bare number. Nothing is carried by colour alone. */
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list {
        list-style: none;
        margin: 0.35rem 0 1.2rem 0;
        padding: 0;
        display: grid;
        grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(24rem, 1fr));
        gap: 0.9rem;
      }
      /* Two tiles across, fixed, inside the full-width summary card.
         Changed from the auto-fill tracks above on 2026-08-18: at a desktop
         width auto-fill gave four or five tiles per row, which spread the
         eight race groups and the six disability types into a wide, dense
         band under the map. Two fixed columns run the same content down the
         page instead, closer to the downloadable report's shape, and give
         each tile enough width that no label wraps past two lines.
         The auto-fill rule above still applies to any city-demo-list that
         appears outside this card. */
      .city-summary-wide ul.city-demo-list {
        grid-template-columns: repeat(2, 1fr);
      }
      /* Below roughly a tablet width two tiles are narrower than the long
         race labels want, so drop to one. The narrow-band figure stacking
         that pairs with this lives after the base tile rules below, so it
         can override them. */
      @media (max-width: 48em) {
        .city-summary-wide ul.city-demo-list {
          grid-template-columns: 1fr;
        }
      }
      /* The figure row is pinned to the bottom of each tile with
         margin-top: auto (the tile is a flex column, and grid stretches
         tiles in a row to equal height), so the percentages line up across
         a row no matter how many lines the label above them takes. This
         replaces an earlier min-height floor on the label, which guessed a
         line count and left a band of empty space -- or lost the alignment
         -- when the browser text size changed. */
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list li.city-demo-tile {
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        background: #faf8f5;
        border: 1px solid #e0dbd2;
        border-left: 4px solid #1c2b3a;
        border-radius: 4px;
        padding: 0.9rem 1.1rem 1rem 1.1rem;
        margin: 0;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-label {
        display: block;
        margin-bottom: 0.7rem;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-term {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.6rem;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.3;
      }
      /* The plain-language gloss that used to sit in parentheses inside the
         label. Roman, not italic (Colin 2026-09-08), and a step down in
         size and contrast so the term reads first. Still inside
         .city-demo-label, so a screen reader announces 'term  gloss' as one
         label with no bracket characters. #3a3a3a on the #faf8f5 tile is
         about 10.6:1, well past WCAG AA for this ~15px text. */
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-desc {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.35rem;
        font-style: normal;
        font-weight: 400;
        color: #3a3a3a;
        line-height: 1.3;
        margin-top: 0.1rem;
      }
      /* Percentage and count side by side, split by a hairline; margin-top:
         auto drops the whole row to the foot of the tile. */
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-figs {
        display: flex;
        align-items: stretch;
        margin-top: auto;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-pct {
        flex: 1 1 0;
        min-width: 0;
        display: flex;
        align-items: center;
        padding-right: 1rem;
        font-size: 3.4rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        line-height: 1.05;
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count {
        flex: 1 1 0;
        min-width: 0;
        display: flex;
        flex-direction: column;
        justify-content: center;
        padding-left: 1.1rem;
        border-left: 1px solid #e0dbd2;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count-val {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.95rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        line-height: 1.1;
        font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums;
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count-unit {
        display: block;
        font-size: 1.3rem;
        font-weight: 400;
        color: #3a3a3a;
        line-height: 1.2;
        margin-top: 0.1rem;
      }
      /* Narrower two-column band (48-62em): shrink the figures so a long
         count and a 3-plus-rem percentage still clear the hairline. */
      @media (min-width: 48.01em) and (max-width: 62em) {
        .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-pct { font-size: 2.9rem; }
        .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count-val { font-size: 1.75rem; }
      }
      /* At or below a tablet width (one tile per row) a half-tile is too
         tight for a 3-plus-rem percentage beside a six-figure count, and
         beside a long share like 0.003%, so the figure row stacks --
         percentage over count, the hairline moving from the side to the
         top. Placed after the base rules above so it overrides them. */
      @media (max-width: 48em) {
        .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-figs {
          flex-direction: column;
          align-items: flex-start;
        }
        .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-pct {
          padding-right: 0;
          font-size: 3.2rem;
        }
        .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count {
          padding-left: 0;
          border-left: 0;
          border-top: 1px solid #e0dbd2;
          margin-top: 0.5rem;
          padding-top: 0.4rem;
          width: 100%;
        }
        .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-count-val {
          font-size: 1.9rem;
        }
      }
      .city-summary ul.city-demo-list .city-demo-na {
        align-self: center;
        font-size: 1.6rem;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #3a3a3a;
      }
      /* Visually hidden, but still read aloud and still found by in-page
         search on most browsers. Standard clip pattern rather than
         display:none, which would remove it from the accessibility tree
         and defeat the purpose. */
      .city-summary .city-demo-sr {
        position: absolute;
        width: 1px;
        height: 1px;
        padding: 0;
        margin: -1px;
        overflow: hidden;
        clip: rect(0, 0, 0, 0);
        clip-path: inset(50%);
        white-space: nowrap;
        border: 0;
      }
      /* Sub-heading above each list (Race / Ethnicity, Sex, Age). Reuses
         the same visual weight as the other <b> sub-headings on this card
         (Employment, Earnings, ...) so the demographics card matches the
         rest of the page now that it no longer relies on a table caption
         for this label. */
      /* Enlarged 1.55rem -> 1.85rem on 2026-08-18. At the old size these
         three labels sat level with the body copy around them and did not
         read as the section breaks they are. 1.85rem keeps them clearly
         below the 2rem h4 above them (Disability Demographics) while
         sitting well above the 1.5rem tile labels below. */
      .city-summary p.city-demo-heading {
        font-size: 1.85rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        letter-spacing: 0.01em;
        margin: 1.4rem 0 0.45rem 0;
      }
      /* The Age note now sits between the Age heading and its tiles, so it
         needs to hug the heading rather than carry the standalone
         paragraph spacing .city-summary-help uses elsewhere. */
      .city-summary p.city-demo-heading + p.city-summary-help {
        margin-top: 0.2rem;
      }
      /* With the card-level h3 headings removed, the first sub-section
         heading sits flush at the top of each card rather than carrying
         the inter-section spacing meant to separate blocks. */
      .city-summary h4:first-child {
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
      }

      /* An equal-height .city-summary-row rule used to live here, making the
         two side-by-side outcome cards flex items so the shorter one did not
         leave a ragged edge. Removed 2026-08-18 along with the col-md-6
         halves themselves: every outcome card is full width now, so no two
         cards ever sit beside each other. */

      /* Full-width demographics card (row two).
         Holds both Disability Demographics and Disability Types. Everything
         inside stacks in a single vertical column at every width. An earlier
         version flowed the longer lists into two CSS columns to use the extra
         width, but two columns of bullets read worse than one, so the lists
         run straight down and the card simply ends where its content ends. */

      /* Full-width explanatory card, used for the Community Living domain,
         which has no city-level indicators available yet. Lighter treatment
         than a data card so it does not read as though data is missing. */
      .city-summary-note {
        background: #faf8f5;
        border-top-width: 3px;
      }
      .city-summary-note h4:first-child {
        margin-top: 0.25rem;
      }

      /* Shared heading above both summary columns. Mirrors .city-summary
         h3 and p, but sits outside the cards so it can span the full
         width and centre over the two-column layout below it. */
      .city-summary-header {
        text-align: center;
        margin: 1.25rem 0 0 0;
        padding: 0 0.5rem;
      }
      .city-summary-header h3 {
        font-size: 2.4rem;
        font-weight: 700;
        margin: 0.25rem 0 0.9rem 0;
        padding-bottom: 0.45rem;
        border-bottom: 2px solid #1c2b3a;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        letter-spacing: -0.01em;
      }
      .city-summary-header p {
        font-size: 1.55rem;
        line-height: 1.75;
        color: #1c1c1c;
        margin: 0 auto;
        max-width: 90ch;
      }

      /* ── Select inputs: font, sizing, and maroon accent on focus ──────── */
      .control-label {
        /* 18px / 600 to match the National Data selector labels. */
        font-size: 18px !important;
        font-weight: 600;
        color: #1c2b3a;
        margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
      }
      .selectize-input,
      .selectize-dropdown,
      .selectize-dropdown-content,
      .selectize-input input,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .active {
        font-size: 19px !important;
      }
      .selectize-input {
        border: 1.5px solid #5c6672 !important;
        border-radius: 4px !important;
        background: #fff !important;
        color: #1c1c1c !important;
        padding: 7px 10px !important;
      }
      .selectize-input.focus,
      .selectize-input:focus-within {
        border-color: #0d3b8e !important;
        box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(13, 59, 142, 0.15) !important;
        outline: none !important;
      }
      .selectize-dropdown {
        border: 1.5px solid #5c6672 !important;
        border-top: none !important;
        border-radius: 0 0 4px 4px !important;
        background: #fff !important;
      }
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option:hover,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .option.active,
      .selectize-dropdown-content .selected {
        background: #013176 !important;
        color: #fff !important;
      }

      /* ── Leaflet legend ─────────────────────────────────────────────── */
      /* Sized in px, not rem: Bootstrap 3 scaffolding sets html font-size to
         10px, so a rem value here renders ~62% of its intended size. The key
         previously read 1.1rem and came out at 11px. */
      .leaflet-container .legend {
        font-size: 17px !important;
        line-height: 1.45 !important;
        color: #1c1c1c !important;
        background: rgba(255,255,255,1.0) !important;
        padding: 12px 16px !important;
        border-radius: 6px !important;
        box-shadow: 0 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.18);
      }
      .leaflet-container .legend .info {
        background: transparent !important;
      }
      /* Legend title sits in a leading div > strong */
      .leaflet-container .legend div strong {
        font-size: 18px !important;
        font-weight: 700 !important;
        display: inline-block;
        margin-bottom: 4px;
      }
      /* Colour swatches: leaflet's inline defaults are 18px squares; scale
         them with the larger text so the key stays legible. The black
         outline keeps the palest bin and the white-ish no-data swatch
         distinguishable from the legend background. */
      .leaflet-container .legend i {
        width: 22px !important;
        height: 22px !important;
        margin-right: 8px !important;
        border: 1px solid #000 !important;
        box-sizing: border-box !important;
      }

      /* Focus ring: maroon to match new palette */
      :focus-visible {
        outline: 3px solid #0d3b8e !important;
        outline-offset: 2px;
      }
    "))
  ),

  tags$main(
    role = "main",

    # ── Page header ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-banner",
      tags$h1("City Data", class = "city-title"),
      tags$p(
        class = "city-note",
        "Select a state and city to explore tract-level disability data and community statistics."
      )
    ),

    # ── Controls card ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-card city-controls-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "City selection controls",
        div(
          class = "city-controls-split",
          div(
            class = "city-controls-row",
            div(
              class = "city-control-field",
              selectInput(
                "state_selector", "Select a state",
                choices  = state_select_choices,
                selected = "Illinois",
                selectize = FALSE,
                width = "100%"
              )
            ),
            div(
              class = "city-control-field",
              # Static native <select>; seeded with the default state's cities,
              # then kept in sync by the observeEvent below (no renderUI remount
              # per state).
              selectInput(
                "city_selector", "Select a city",
                choices  = initial_city_choices,
                selected = if ("Chicago" %in% initial_city_choices) "Chicago" else initial_city_choices[1],
                selectize = FALSE,
                width = "100%"
              )
            )
          ),
          tags$section(
            `aria-label` = "Download the selected city",
            class = "city-control-action",
            downloadButton(
              "download_city",
              "Download",
              class        = "btn-download-city",
              icon         = dl_icon(),
              `aria-label` = "Download the selected city as an accessible, print-ready ADA-PARC report: map and key, then summary tables for people with disabilities in this city"
            )
          )
        ),
        # Visually hidden live region: names the state, how many cities it has,
        # and the city now shown. Mirrors national_selection_status so the two
        # tabs give screen-reader users the same feedback on a change.
        div(
          class = "city-sr-only",
          role  = "status",
          `aria-live` = "polite",
          textOutput("city_selection_status", inline = TRUE)
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Map card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-card city-map-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "City tract map showing disability rates",
        fluidRow(
          column(12, div(`aria-live` = "polite", withSpinner(uiOutput("city_map_title")))),
          column(12, withSpinner(leafletOutput("snapshotmap", height = 550)))
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Summary card ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    div(
      class = "city-card city-data-summary-card",
      tags$section(
        role = "region",
        `aria-label` = "City summary statistics for people with disabilities",
        fluidRow(
          column(12, div(`aria-live` = "polite", withSpinner(uiOutput("city_summary"))))
        )
      )
    ),

    # ── Footer note ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    tags$p(
      class = "city-note city-note-footer",
      # Coverage wording corrected 31 July 2026. The previous text attributed
      # missing values to a population threshold of 30,000, which is wrong:
      # 1,322 selectable cities exceed that population but only 648 carry the
      # education and commuting measures. The Census rule keys on the size of
      # the population with disabilities, with the cutoff falling between
      # 7,178 and 7,883 residents across the 8,407 places in the file.
      "Note: Some measures are not published for every city. The Census releases the education and commuting figures only where the population with disabilities is large enough, roughly 7,500 residents, so those two sections are shown for 648 of the cities in this tool and hidden for the rest. Other Not Applicable or NA values may appear where a figure was suppressed for that city. Percentages built on a small population count, such as a race or ethnicity group of only a few dozen residents in a given city, can shift dramatically based on a handful of survey responses and carry a wide margin of error, so treat figures drawn from small subgroups with caution."
    )
  )
  , adaparc_footer
)

# ----------------------------
# Server
# ----------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  # --- State selection ---
  state_selected <- reactive({
    req(input$state_selector)
    state_abbr <- state_choices[[input$state_selector]]
    req(!is.null(state_abbr))
    state_abbr
  })

  # --- City choices for selected state ---
  # May be empty for a place with no non-CDP cities; the req() in city_selected()
  # (and updateSelectInput leaving the control empty) is the guard downstream, so
  # this no longer req()s on row count and the status line can report "0".
  city_choices <- reactive({
    req(state_selected())
    dict_location_crosswalk %>%
      filter(state == state_selected(), !str_detect(place_NAME, " CDP")) %>%
      distinct(place_NAME, place_GEOID) %>%
      # Order by city NAME. The old `deframe() %>% sort()` sorted by the GEOID
      # values, so the list came out in an arbitrary-looking order — tolerable
      # with selectize's search box, confusing in a plain <select>.
      arrange(place_NAME) %>%
      tibble::deframe()
  })

  # Keep the static #city_selector <select> in sync with the chosen state.
  # Fires once on startup (ignoreInit = FALSE) to populate the initial list.
  observeEvent(input$state_selector, {
    cities <- names(city_choices())
    updateSelectInput(
      session, "city_selector",
      choices  = cities,
      selected = if ("Chicago" %in% cities) "Chicago" else cities[1]
    )
  })

  # Visually hidden status line for the selection controls: active state, how
  # many cities it offers, and which city is shown. Worded distinctly from the
  # map/summary aria-live regions so they don't read on top of each other.
  output$city_selection_status <- renderText({
    req(state_selected())
    cities <- names(city_choices())
    n_cities <- length(cities)
    state_lbl <- input$state_selector %||% "the selected state"
    if (n_cities == 0) {
      sprintf("%s selected. No cities available for this location.", state_lbl)
    } else {
      current <- if (!is.null(input$city_selector) && nzchar(input$city_selector)) {
        input$city_selector
      } else {
        cities[1]
      }
      sprintf(
        "%s selected. %d cit%s available. Now showing %s.",
        state_lbl, n_cities, if (n_cities == 1) "y" else "ies", current
      )
    }
  })
  outputOptions(output, "city_selection_status", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

  # --- City selected GEOID ---
  city_selected <- reactive({
    req(input$city_selector, city_choices())
    selected_city <- city_choices()[input$city_selector]
    req(!is.null(selected_city))
    selected_city
  })

  # --- Place-level data for the selected city ---
  city_place <- reactive({
    req(city_selected())
    city_data <- city_place_full %>% filter(GEOID == city_selected())
    req(nrow(city_data) > 0)
    city_data
  })

  # --- Tract SF and tract data for selected city ---
  city_tract_sf <- reactive({
    req(city_selected())
    tract_ids <- dict_location_crosswalk %>%
      filter(place_GEOID %in% city_selected()) %>%
      pull(tract_GEOID)
    req(length(tract_ids) > 0)
    tracts_sf %>% filter(tract_GEOID %in% tract_ids)
  })

  city_tract <- reactive({
    req(city_selected())
    tract_ids <- dict_location_crosswalk %>%
      filter(place_GEOID %in% city_selected()) %>%
      pull(tract_GEOID)
    req(length(tract_ids) > 0)
    tracts_data %>% filter(GEOID %in% tract_ids)
  })

  # --- City map title ---
  output$city_map_title <- renderUI({
    req(city_place())
    title <- city_place() %>%
      mutate(NAME = str_replace_all(NAME, " (city|village|municipality|town), ", ", ")) %>%
      pull(NAME)
    div(h4(title, class = "city-map-title"))
  })

  # ----------------------------
  # MAP: fixed national classification + leaflet render
  #
  # Place these EXACTLY here: after city_tract()/city_tract_sf() reactives exist,
  # and before output$city_summary.
  #
  # city_map_breaks / city_map_labels are FIXED (computed once at app start
  # from the full national tract distribution -- see setup chunk). Only the
  # 4 discrete colors are reactive to the user's palette choice.
  # ----------------------------

  city_map_colors <- reactive({
    raw_palette <- access_map_palette_selected()
    if (is.function(raw_palette)) raw_palette(4) else brewer.pal(4, raw_palette)
  })

  # ── Shared tract map data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for BOTH the interactive Leaflet map below and the
  # static print map built for the "Download Selected City" report
  # (render_city_tract_map() in scripts/functions.R, called from the download
  # handler further down). Both read this same joined, binned, colored data,
  # so the printed map can never land in a different bin or a different
  # colour than the one shown on screen. Was previously computed inline
  # inside output$snapshotmap only; pulled out so the download handler can
  # read it too without a second join-and-bin pass.
  city_map_data <- reactive({
    req(city_tract_sf(), city_tract())

    sf_df <- city_tract_sf() %>%
      mutate(tract_id_norm = normalize_tract_geoid(tract_GEOID))

    tab_df <- city_tract() %>%
      transmute(
        tract_id_norm = normalize_tract_geoid(GEOID),
        pct_cni_total_dis_place = pct_cni_total_dis_place   # already dbl 0–100
      )

    data <- left_join(sf_df, tab_df, by = "tract_id_norm")
    has_any_data <- any(!is.na(data$pct_cni_total_dis_place))

    map_colors   <- city_map_colors()
    map_na_color <- access_map_na_selected()

    data <- data %>%
      mutate(
        pct_cat = cut(
          pct_cni_total_dis_place,
          breaks         = city_map_breaks,
          include.lowest = TRUE,
          labels         = city_map_labels
        ),
        # No-data tracts take the no-data colour belonging to the SELECTED
        # palette, not a fixed grey. Under High Contrast Mono a grey would be
        # only 6.5 CIEDE2000 units from the lightest band, so "no data" would
        # read as "best". See the NO-DATA note in scripts/palettes.R.
        fill_col = dplyr::case_when(
          is.na(pct_cat) ~ map_na_color,
          TRUE           ~ map_colors[as.integer(pct_cat)]
        )
      )

    # Append a "No data" key ONLY when some tract actually lacks a value, so
    # the legend never explains a colour that is not on the map. This matters
    # more now that the no-data colour varies by palette: under High Contrast
    # Mono it is blue, which is unexplained otherwise.
    has_gaps   <- any(is.na(data$pct_cni_total_dis_place))
    leg_colors <- if (has_gaps) c(map_colors, map_na_color) else map_colors
    leg_labels <- if (has_gaps) c(city_map_labels, "No data") else city_map_labels

    list(
      data         = data,
      has_any_data = has_any_data,
      has_gaps     = has_gaps,
      leg_colors   = leg_colors,
      leg_labels   = leg_labels
    )
  })

  output$snapshotmap <- renderLeaflet({
    md   <- city_map_data()
    data <- md$data

    m <- leaflet(data) %>%
      # Muted, high-contrast neutral basemap (light gray / white) so the
      # tract choropleth does the color work and the map remains
      # accessible. CartoDB.Positron is WCAG-friendly and keeps labels
      # legible against any palette.
      addProviderTiles(
        providers$CartoDB.Positron,
        options = providerTileOptions(opacity = 0.9)
      ) %>%
      addResetMapButton() %>%
      addPolygons(
        stroke = TRUE, color = "#1c2b3a", weight = 1, smoothFactor = 0,
        fillColor = ~fill_col,
        fillOpacity = 0.82,
        layerId = ~tract_GEOID,
        label = ~lapply(ifelse(
          is.na(pct_cni_total_dis_place),
          paste0("<b>Tract ", tract_GEOID, "</b><br/>No data available"),
          paste0("<b>Tract ", tract_GEOID, "</b><br/>",
                 round(pct_cni_total_dis_place, 1), "% with disability")
        ), htmltools::HTML),
        labelOptions = labelOptions(
          style = list("font-weight" = "normal", padding = "3px 8px"),
          textsize = "13px",
          direction = "auto"
        ),
        highlight = highlightOptions(
          weight = 2.5,
          color = "#222222",
          fillOpacity = 0.95,
          bringToFront = TRUE
        )
      ) %>%
      addSearchOSM(
        options = searchOptions(
          autoCollapse = FALSE, minLength = 3, position = "topleft",
          zoom = 15, autoResize = FALSE, hideMarkerOnCollapse = TRUE
        )
      )
      # No addEasyprint() here. The map previously carried its own "Download
      # map as PNG" control; that affordance is now consolidated into the
      # single "Download Selected City" button in the controls card (see
      # output$download_city below), which produces the full branded,
      # accessible, print-ready report rather than a bare PNG of the map
      # alone. Per-map download intentionally removed, not just unused.

    if (md$has_any_data) {
      m <- m %>%
        addLegend(
          position = "topright",
          colors   = md$leg_colors,
          labels   = md$leg_labels,
          opacity  = 0.82,
          title    = "% With Disability"
        )
    } else {
      m <- m %>%
        addControl(
          html = paste0(
            "<div style='background: rgba(255,255,255,0.92); padding: 6px 8px; border-radius: 4px;'>",
            "<b>% With Disability</b><br/>No tract values joined (tract GEOID mismatch).",
            "</div>"
          ),
          position = "topright"
        )
    }

    m
  })

  # ----------------------------
  # City Summary Output
  # ----------------------------
  # ── Shared city profile bundle ────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Single source of truth for BOTH the on-screen summary card and the
  # downloadable full city report. Every fragment below (race_ethnicity,
  # sex, age_groups, ...) is built exactly once here via the same
  # render_demo_list() / render_comparison_table() helpers the page always
  # used, and both output$city_summary and the "Download Selected City"
  # handler read the same list, so the download can never drift from what is
  # on screen. Mirrors national_topic_bundle() in the National Data app above.
  city_download_bundle <- reactive({
    req(city_place())

    # Cleaned "City, State" title, shared by the map heading (output$city_map_title
    # applies the same transform separately) and this bundle's print title.
    full_title <- city_place() %>%
      mutate(NAME = str_replace_all(NAME, " (city|village|municipality|town), ", ", ")) %>%
      pull(NAME)

    introductory_text <- paste0(
      "Based on ACS 2024 5-Year Estimates, of the city's <b>", fmt_num(city_place()$pop_cni_total_all),
      "</b> residents, <b>", fmt_num(city_place()$pop_cni_total_dis_place),
      "</b> (<b>", fmt_pct_1dp(city_place()$pct_cni_total_dis_place), "</b>) are people with disabilities."
    )
    # The trailing <br><br> this string used to carry was spacing the lead
    # sentence off the block below it. Now that the sentence sits in its own
    # centred header, the paragraph margin handles that.

    # Explanatory / methodological notes, named once here rather than as
    # literals inside the paste0 assembly below, so the downloadable report
    # can quote the exact same sentences rather than a second hand-copied
    # version that could drift from the on-screen wording over time.
    #
    # Defined ahead of the section fragments rather than after them (where it
    # sat until 2026-08-18) because render_demo_list() now takes age_intro as
    # an argument, so the Age note travels inside the Age fragment to both
    # consumers instead of each one placing it separately.
    help <- list(
      demographics_intro = paste0(
        "For each Race/Ethnicity, Sex, and Age group below, the headline ",
        "figure is that group's share of the city's total population, with ",
        "the number of people that represents shown underneath it. ",
        "Hispanic/Latino is an ethnicity that can include people of any ",
        "race, so it overlaps with the race categories above it, and ",
        "figures across groups are not meant to sum to the city total."
      ),
      age_intro = paste0(
        "The Census asks about hearing and vision difficulty at every age, ",
        "but the other four disability types (cognitive, ambulatory, ",
        "self-care, and independent living) are only asked starting at age ",
        "5, and independent living only from age 15. The “Under 5” ",
        "figure below reflects hearing and vision difficulty alone, so it ",
        "is not directly comparable to the other age groups, which draw on ",
        "more disability types."
      ),
      disability_types_intro = paste0(
        "Each percentage below is the share of the city's total population, ",
        "not just the population with disabilities, that reports that ",
        "specific type of disability. A person can have more than one type, ",
        "and many do, so these categories overlap. The six figures below ",
        "will add up to more than the city's overall disability rate, often ",
        "to about twice it, and are not meant to sum to the total."
      ),
      outcomes_intro = paste0(
        "Each indicator below is shown for residents with disabilities ",
        "beside residents without disabilities, so the two can be compared ",
        "directly."
      ),
      health_insurance = paste0(
        "A person can hold public and private coverage at the same time, ",
        "so those two figures are not meant to sum to the any-coverage figure."
      ),
      earnings = paste0(
        "Median earnings in the past 12 months among residents ages 16 and ",
        "over who had earnings. This is pay from work only. It does not ",
        "include Social Security, disability benefits or investment income, ",
        "and it leaves out residents who did not work, so it is not a ",
        "measure of total income."
      ),
      poverty = paste0(
        "Living below the federal poverty line. As of 2024, that is a ",
        "yearly income below $14,891 for an individual or $29,678 for a ",
        "family of four."
      ),
      housing_burden = paste0(
        "Citywide figures for all households, not disability specific. A ",
        "disability specific breakdown is not published at the city level, ",
        "so there is no comparison to show here."
      ),
      housing_access = paste0(
        "Among households in each HUD-assisted housing program, the share ",
        "with a head of household or spouse/co-head who has a disability. ",
        "This is a rate within an already-assisted population, not a ",
        "citywide figure, so it should not be compared directly to the ",
        "disability rate shown elsewhere on this page. A missing figure ",
        "usually means the city has no households reported in that ",
        "program, not a suppressed or unpublished value."
      )
      # TEMPORARILY DISABLED 2026-08-17: paired with the cil_distance block
      # above. Re-enable once cil_weighted_mean_distance_mi is available.
      # ,
      # cil_distance = paste0(
      #   "The average straight-line distance a resident with a disability ",
      #   "would need to travel to reach the closest Center for Independent ",
      #   "Living, weighted by where people with disabilities live within ",
      #   "the city. This is straight-line distance, not travel time or a ",
      #   "road route. The nearest center by distance is not always the one ",
      #   "that serves this city: Centers for Independent Living have ",
      #   "defined service areas, usually by county or region."
      # )
    )

    race_ethnicity <- render_demo_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        demo_row("White alone (non-Hispanic)", "pop_cni_whitenonhisp_dis"),
        demo_row("Black/African American",     "pop_cni_black_dis"),
        demo_row("American Indian/Alaska Native", "pop_cni_aian_dis"),
        demo_row("Asian",                       "pop_cni_asian_dis"),
        demo_row("Native Hawaiian/Other Pacific Islander", "pop_cni_nhopi_dis"),
        demo_row("Some other race(s) identified", "pop_cni_raceother_dis"),
        demo_row("Two or more races",           "pop_cni_racemulti_dis"),
        demo_row("Hispanic/Latino (any race)",  "pop_cni_hisp_dis")
      ),
      "Race / Ethnicity"
    )

    sex <- render_demo_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        demo_row("Male",   "pop_cni_male_dis"),
        demo_row("Female", "pop_cni_female_dis")
      ),
      "Sex"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Age
    #
    # Same two-figure list as Race/Ethnicity and Sex, via render_demo_list():
    # count and share of the total population.
    #
    # Four bands, not three. An earlier version of this comment claimed
    # disability is "never recorded" under age 5 and dropped that band
    # entirely -- that was wrong. The ACS asks hearing and vision
    # difficulty at every age, including under 5; only the other four
    # types (cognitive, ambulatory, self-care, and independent living,
    # the last restricted to age 15+) start at age 5. Census still
    # publishes an official "has a disability" aggregate for under-5
    # children from the two types it does ask, and the pipeline carries
    # it as pop_cni_under5_dis_place, same numerator pattern as every
    # other band. Confirmed against city_place_full.Rds: the four bands
    # below sum exactly to pop_cni_total_dis_place for Los Angeles
    # (441,455 = 441,455); the three-band version was short by exactly
    # the under-5 count.
    #
    # Because the under-5 count is built from only 2 of the 6 disability
    # types while every other band draws on all 6 (or 5, for ages 5-14),
    # its share of the total population is not on the same footing as the
    # other bands -- a lower under-5 share does not mean disability is
    # rarer at that age, only that fewer question types apply. The help
    # text below the list says so.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    age_groups <- render_demo_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        demo_row("Under 5",            "pop_cni_under5_dis_place"),
        demo_row("Ages 5 to 17",       "pop_cni_5to17_dis_place"),
        demo_row("Ages 18 to 64",      "pop_cni_18to64_dis_place"),
        demo_row("Ages 65 and older",  "pop_cni_65plus_dis_place")
      ),
      "Age",
      # Sits between the "Age" heading and the tiles. It used to be emitted
      # separately by each consumer, above the heading, where it read as a
      # closing note on Sex rather than an introduction to Age.
      note = help$age_intro
    )

    # Stat tiles, matching Race/Ethnicity, Sex and Age, per Colin's
    # 2026-08-18 request. The returned fragment is a complete
    # <ul class="city-demo-list">, so neither consumer wraps it in a <ul>
    # of its own any more. Labels keep the plain-language gloss the bullet
    # version carried in parentheses; demo_label_html() lifts it out of the
    # brackets onto its own line as .city-demo-desc.
    disability_types <- render_type_list(
      city_place(),
      list(
        type_row("Hearing",
                 "pop_cni_total_hearing_dis",   "pct_cni_total_hearing_dis"),
        type_row("Vision",
                 "pop_cni_total_vision_dis",    "pct_cni_total_vision_dis"),
        type_row("Cognitive",
                 "pop_cni_total_cognitive_dis", "pct_cni_total_cognitive_dis"),
        type_row("Ambulatory (difficulty walking or climbing stairs)",
                 "pop_cni_total_mobility_dis",  "pct_cni_total_mobility_dis"),
        type_row("Self Care (difficulty bathing or dressing)",
                 "pop_cni_selfcare_dis",        "pct_cni_selfcare_dis"),
        type_row("Independent Living (difficulty doing errands alone)",
                 "pop_cni_indepliving_dis",     "pct_cni_indepliving_dis")
      )
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Outcome indicators, paired with/without disability
    #
    # From here to the housing-burden block, every indicator is rendered as a
    # two-column comparison table via render_comparison_table(). cp is the
    # single-row city data frame the specs read from.
    #
    # Housing cost burden is the one exception and stays a bullet list: it
    # comes from B25070 and B25091, which are household tables with no
    # disability dimension, so there is no comparison to draw.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    cp <- city_place()

    employment <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Employed, part or full time",
                "pct_cni_18to64_employed_dis",   "pct_cni_18to64_employed_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_employed_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_employed_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Unemployed, looking for work",
                "pct_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis", "pct_cni_18to64_nodis_unemployed",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_unemployed_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Out of the labor force",
                "pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_dis",   "pct_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_notlabor_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_notlabor_nodis")
      ),
      "Labor force status, ages 18 to 64"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Earnings
    #
    # ACS B18140. Note the dictionary calls these variables "Median
    # Individual Income", but B18140 measures median EARNINGS, meaning pay
    # from work only, over a universe restricted to people who had
    # earnings. It excludes benefits, Social Security, SSI and investment
    # income, so it is not individual income in the ordinary sense. The
    # labels below say earnings; the dictionary entry should be corrected
    # to match.
    #
    # Coverage: the disabled figure resolves for 4,821 of the 5,881
    # non-CDP places in the selector, and the non-disabled figure is
    # present for all but two of those, so the pair travels together.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    earnings <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Median earnings, ages 16 and over",
                "pop_cni_16plus_medincome_dis", "pop_cni_16plus_medincome_nodis",
                kind = "dollar")
      ),
      "Median earnings among residents who had earnings"
    )

    poverty <- render_comparison_table(
      cp,
      list(
        cmp_row("Children under 18",
                "pct_cni_under18_poverty_dis", "pct_cni_under18_poverty_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_under18_poverty_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_under18_poverty_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Adults 18 to 64",
                "pct_cni_18to64_poverty_dis",  "pct_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_poverty_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_18to64_poverty_nodis"),
        cmp_row("Adults 65 and older",
                "pct_cni_65plus_poverty_dis",  "pct_cni_65plus_poverty_nodis",
                dis_pop = "pop_cni_65plus_poverty_dis",
                nodis_pop = "pop_cni_65plus_poverty_nodis")
      ),
      "Residents living below the federal poverty line"
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Health insurance, split by age band
    #
    # The 19-64 band was already shown. The 65+ band is the same four
    # measures and is populated for 8,372 of 8,407 places, so it is shown
    # alongside rather than gated. "Any coverage" is listed first because
    # private and public overlap and will not sum to it.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------
```
