# Category display order, matching the ADA-PARC outcome domains used across the
# rest of the site.
fs_categories <- c("Community Living", "Work & Economic", "Community Participation")

# Slug for data-* hooks and element ids: same transform the category tabs used
# before, plus a trim of any leading / trailing dash.
fs_slug <- function(x) gsub("(^-|-$)", "", gsub("[^a-z0-9]+", "-", tolower(x)))

fs_in_category <- function(cat) Filter(function(s) s$category == cat, fact_sheets)
fs_clusters_of <- function(sheets) unique(vapply(sheets, function(s) s$cluster, character(1)))

# ── Layout: landing → area → reader ─────────────────────────────────────
# Three screens in one centred column; only one is ever in the visible state,
# the other two carry [hidden] (which also drops them from the a11y tree, so
# exactly one <h1> is exposed at a time):
#
#   1. Landing (#fs_home)  — masthead + three upright "area" cards, one per
#      ADA-PARC outcome domain. Each card is a <button> with a matching line
#      symbol. A Download-All button and the ADA-PARC brand mark sit at the
#      foot.
#   2. Area (#fs_area)      — the chosen domain's sheets only, grouped under
#      topic-cluster <h2>s as a roomy vertical list of <button> rows. Built
#      on demand from a small JSON copy of the registry.
#   3. Reader (#fs_reader)  — a back control, download / open actions and the
#      sheet itself in one lazy <iframe>. Only one sheet is ever in the DOM.
#
# Navigation is a self-contained in-memory state machine (showHome / showArea /
# showReader) — NOT the History API. This sub-app is an embedded shinyApp(), i.e.
# an iframe that shares its session history with the surrounding flexdashboard
# site; driving screen state through history.pushState / history.back() let a
# Back click walk past the app's own entries onto another site tab (the
# Scorecard). The in-app Back controls now move reader → area → home directly;
# the browser / device Back button leaves the Fact Sheets tab, as it does from
# every other tab. Forward moves send focus to the destination <h1>
# (tabindex=-1); Back restores focus to the card / row that opened the screen
# being left. An aria-live region names each screen change.
#
# This replaces the filtered card grid that showed all 25 sheets at once: the
# landing now asks one question — which domain? — with large targets, and no
# sheet list appears until the set is down to 2–12. The lists stay plain
# <ul>/<button>; a 25-item tablist would be an ARIA anti-pattern.
#
# Chrome is the site's NAVY palette on warm off-white, the same framing the
# scorecards use — deliberately NOT the sheet's own maroon/gold, so the colour
# break tells the reader the framed document is a separate thing. Gold stays
# absent from the chrome. There is no dark theme; the sub-app palette is fixed.
#
# ALL SIZES ARE IN px, NOT rem. fluidPage() loads Bootstrap 3, whose
# scaffolding sets html { font-size: 10px }, so rem in a sub-app style block
# resolves against a 10px root. See project memory "Bootstrap 3 rem Trap".

# One matched set of line symbols, one per outcome domain. Decorative:
# aria-hidden + focusable=false in the markup, so the button's own text and
# aria-label carry the meaning.
fs_symbols <- list(
  "Community Living" = HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 48 48" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><path d="M7 22 24 7l17 15"/><path d="M11 20v20h26V20"/><path d="M20 40v-10h8v10"/></svg>'),
  "Work & Economic" = HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 48 48" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><rect x="7" y="15" width="34" height="24" rx="3"/><path d="M18 15v-3.5A3.5 3.5 0 0 1 21.5 8h5A3.5 3.5 0 0 1 30 11.5V15"/><path d="M7 26h34"/><path d="M21.5 24h5v4h-5z"/></svg>'),
  "Community Participation" = HTML('<svg viewBox="0 0 48 48" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"><circle cx="24" cy="15" r="5"/><path d="M14 39c0-6 4.5-10 10-10s10 4 10 10"/><circle cx="9.5" cy="20" r="3.6"/><path d="M3.5 35c0-4.2 2.7-7.4 6.4-7.9"/><circle cx="38.5" cy="20" r="3.6"/><path d="M44.5 35c0-4.2-2.7-7.4-6.4-7.9"/></svg>')
)

# Registry reshaped for the client:
#   { slug: { name, clusters: [ { name, sheets: [ {file,title,sub,desc} ] } ] } }
# jsonlite::unbox keeps every scalar a JSON string and every list a JSON array,
# so a future single-sheet cluster still serialises as an array.
fs_client_data <- setNames(
  lapply(fs_categories, function(cat) {
    sheets <- fs_in_category(cat)
    list(
      name = jsonlite::unbox(cat),
      clusters = lapply(fs_clusters_of(sheets), function(cl) {
        list(
          name = jsonlite::unbox(cl),
          sheets = lapply(Filter(function(s) s$cluster == cl, sheets), function(s) {
            list(
              file  = jsonlite::unbox(s$file),
              title = jsonlite::unbox(s$title),
              sub   = jsonlite::unbox(s$subtitle),
              desc  = jsonlite::unbox(s$desc)
            )
          })
        )
      })
    )
  }),
  vapply(fs_categories, fs_slug, character(1))
)
fs_data_json <- as.character(jsonlite::toJSON(fs_client_data))

ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$head(
    tags$style(HTML("
      /* EB Garamond: declared here because shinyApp() sub-apps render in an
         isolated context where the parent flexdashboard www/styles.css does
         not reliably cascade into the rendered content. */
      *, *::before, *::after { font-family: 'EB Garamond', Garamond, Georgia, serif !important; }
      body { background: #f9f7f4; margin: 0; }
      /* [hidden] is display:none in the UA sheet, which any author `display`
         declaration overrides, so it is restated here. */
      [hidden] { display: none !important; }

      /* ---- palette: site navy on warm off-white; committed light ---- */
      .fs-wrap {
        --page: #f9f7f4; --surface: #ffffff; --surface-2: #f5f8fc;
        --ink: #1c2b3a; --mute: #4a5560;
        --navy: #013176; --navy-deep: #01214f;
        --rule: #e4e8ef; --rule-strong: #c9d3e0;
        --focus: #0d3b8e; --shadow: 0 1px 5px rgba(28,43,58,.08);
        max-width: 1040px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 26px 24px 72px; color: var(--ink);
      }
      .fs-wrap :focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; }

      /* ---- masthead ---- */
      .fs-mast { margin-bottom: 4px; }
      .fs-heading { font-size: 34px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--ink); margin: 0; letter-spacing: -.01em; }
      .fs-rule { width: 72px; height: 3px; background: var(--navy); margin: 12px 0 14px; }
      .fs-subheading { font-size: 18px; color: var(--ink); margin: 0; line-height: 1.55; max-width: 60ch; }

      /* ---- landing: three upright area cards ---- */
      .fs-areas { margin-top: 40px; }
      .fs-vgrid {
        list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0;
        display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 18px;
      }
      .fs-vcard {
        width: 100%; min-height: 300px;
        display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; text-align: center;
        background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 20px;
        padding: 40px 26px 32px; cursor: pointer; font-family: inherit; color: var(--ink);
        transition: border-color .16s ease, transform .16s ease, box-shadow .16s ease;
      }
      .fs-vcard:hover { border-color: var(--navy); transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 14px 34px -20px rgba(1,49,118,.42); }
      .fs-vcard-title { font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--navy); line-height: 1.16; letter-spacing: -.01em; max-width: 11ch; }
      .fs-vcard-bar { width: 24px; height: 2px; background: var(--navy); opacity: .32; margin: 15px 0 18px; flex: none; }
      .fs-vcard-sym { color: var(--navy); width: 44px; height: 44px; }
      .fs-vcard-sym svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; display: block; }
      .fs-vcard-spacer { flex: 1 1 auto; }
      .fs-vcard-go {
        margin-top: 26px; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--navy);
        background: var(--surface); border: 1.6px solid var(--navy); border-radius: 999px; padding: 10px 24px;
        transition: background .16s ease, color .16s ease;
      }
      .fs-vcard:hover .fs-vcard-go,
      .fs-vcard:focus-visible .fs-vcard-go { background: var(--navy); color: #fff; }

      /* ---- landing foot: Download All + brand mark ---- */
      .fs-home-foot {
        display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 18px 24px; flex-wrap: wrap;
        margin-top: 44px; padding-top: 26px; border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
      }
      .fs-dl-all {
        font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; color: #fff; text-decoration: none; display: inline-block;
        background: var(--navy); border: 1.6px solid var(--navy); border-radius: 999px; padding: 13px 30px;
        transition: background .16s ease, border-color .16s ease;
      }
      .fs-dl-all:hover, .fs-dl-all:focus-visible { background: var(--navy-deep); border-color: var(--navy-deep); color: #fff; }
      .fs-brand { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 15px; }
      .fs-brand-word { height: 46px; width: auto; display: block; }
      .fs-brand-icon { height: 34px; width: 34px; border-radius: 7px; display: block; }

      /* ---- area screen ---- */
      .fs-area-title { font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--navy); margin: 14px 0 0; line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -.01em; }
      .fs-area-sub { font-size: 16px; color: var(--mute); margin: 10px 0 0; }
      .fs-cluster { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--mute); margin: 34px 0 14px; }
      .fs-rows { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 14px; }
      .fs-row {
        width: 100%; text-align: left; font-family: inherit; cursor: pointer; color: var(--ink);
        background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 16px;
        padding: 26px 30px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 24px;
        transition: border-color .16s ease, transform .16s ease;
      }
      .fs-row:hover { border-color: var(--navy); transform: translateX(4px); }
      .fs-row-x { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 7px; min-width: 0; }
      .fs-row-t { font-size: 21px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--navy); line-height: 1.18; }
      .fs-row-d { font-size: 15px; color: var(--mute); line-height: 1.5; max-width: 64ch; }
      .fs-row-go { font-size: 22px; color: var(--navy); opacity: .4; flex: none; transition: opacity .16s ease; }
      .fs-row:hover .fs-row-go { opacity: 1; }

      /* ---- back control (area + reader) ---- */
      .fs-back {
        font-family: inherit; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--navy);
        background: none; border: 0; cursor: pointer; padding: 6px 2px;
      }
      .fs-back:hover { text-decoration: underline; }

      /* ---- reader ---- */
      .fs-reader { margin-top: 8px; }
      .fs-reader-title { font-size: 22px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--navy); margin: 6px 0 2px; line-height: 1.25; }
      .fs-reader-actions { display: flex; gap: 10px; flex-wrap: wrap; margin: 10px 0 14px; }
      .fs-btn-dl, .fs-btn-open {
        font-family: inherit; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; border-radius: 6px;
        padding: 9px 18px; cursor: pointer; text-decoration: none; display: inline-block;
        border: 1.5px solid var(--navy); line-height: 1.4;
      }
      .fs-btn-dl { background: var(--navy); color: #fff; }
      .fs-btn-dl:hover, .fs-btn-dl:focus { background: var(--navy-deep); border-color: var(--navy-deep); color: #fff; text-decoration: none; }
      .fs-btn-open { background: var(--surface); color: var(--navy); }
      .fs-btn-open:hover, .fs-btn-open:focus { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--navy); text-decoration: none; }
      #fs_frame {
        display: block; width: 100%; height: 78vh; min-height: 560px;
        border: 1px solid var(--rule); border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; box-shadow: var(--shadow);
      }

      /* ---- screen-reader-only ---- */
      .fs-sr-only {
        position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; padding: 0; margin: -1px;
        overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; border: 0;
      }

      @media (max-width: 860px) {
        .fs-vgrid { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
        .fs-vcard { min-height: 0; padding: 32px 24px; }
        .fs-row { padding: 20px 20px; }
      }
      @media (max-width: 760px) { #fs_frame { height: 72vh; } }
      @media (max-width: 620px) {
        .fs-wrap { padding: 20px 14px 44px; }
        .fs-heading { font-size: 28px; }
        .fs-subheading { font-size: 17px; }
        .fs-area-title { font-size: 25px; }
        .fs-reader-actions { flex-direction: column; }
        /* On a phone the inline iframe is the least comfortable way to read a
           sheet, so surface the open-in-new-tab action first. */
        #fs_open { order: -1; }
        .fs-btn-dl, .fs-btn-open { text-align: center; }
      }
      @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .fs-wrap * { transition: none !important; } }
    "))
  ),

  div(class = "fs-wrap",

    # ---- screen 1: landing ----
    tags$div(id = "fs_home",
      tags$div(class = "fs-mast",
        h1(class = "fs-heading", id = "fs_home_h", tabindex = "-1", "ADA-PARC Fact Sheets"),
        tags$div(class = "fs-rule", `aria-hidden` = "true"),
        p(class = "fs-subheading",
          "Short, plain-language briefs on single disability outcomes. Choose an area to begin.")
      ),
      tags$nav(class = "fs-areas", `aria-label` = "Fact sheet areas",
        tags$ul(class = "fs-vgrid", role = "list",
          lapply(fs_categories, function(cat) {
            tags$li(
              tags$button(type = "button", class = "fs-vcard", `data-cat` = fs_slug(cat),
                `aria-label` = sprintf("%s — %d fact sheets", cat, length(fs_in_category(cat))),
                tags$span(class = "fs-vcard-title", cat),
                tags$span(class = "fs-vcard-bar", `aria-hidden` = "true"),
                tags$span(class = "fs-vcard-sym", `aria-hidden` = "true", fs_symbols[[cat]]),
                tags$span(class = "fs-vcard-spacer", `aria-hidden` = "true"),
                tags$span(class = "fs-vcard-go", `aria-hidden` = "true", HTML("View &rarr;"))
              )
            )
          })
        )
      ),
      tags$div(class = "fs-home-foot",
        tags$a(class = "fs-dl-all", href = "factsheets/adaparc-factsheets.zip",
          download = "adaparc-factsheets.zip",
          "Download All",
          tags$span(class = "fs-sr-only",
            sprintf(" — all %d fact sheets as a ZIP archive", length(fact_sheets)))),
        tags$span(class = "fs-brand",
          tags$img(class = "fs-brand-word", src = "brand/PARC_blue_text.png",
            alt = "ADA-PARC", width = "78", height = "46"),
          tags$img(class = "fs-brand-icon", src = "brand/PARC_blue_icon.png",
            alt = "", width = "34", height = "34")
        )
      )
    ),

    # ---- screen 2: area (heading, sub and rows populated on demand) ----
    tags$div(id = "fs_area", hidden = NA,
      tags$button(class = "fs-back", type = "button", id = "fs_area_back",
        `aria-label` = "Back to all fact sheet areas", HTML("&larr; All areas")),
      h1(class = "fs-area-title", id = "fs_area_h", tabindex = "-1",
         `aria-describedby` = "fs_area_sub", ""),
      p(class = "fs-area-sub", id = "fs_area_sub", ""),
      tags$div(id = "fs_area_body")
    ),

    # ---- screen 3: reader (hidden until a sheet is chosen) ----
    tags$div(id = "fs_reader", class = "fs-reader", hidden = NA,
      tags$button(class = "fs-back", type = "button", id = "fs_back", HTML("&larr; Back")),
      # h1 for the reader screen: the other two screens are fully hidden while
      # this is shown, so exactly one h1 is ever exposed.
      h1(class = "fs-reader-title", id = "fs_title", tabindex = "-1",
         `aria-describedby` = "fs_desc", ""),
      p(class = "fs-sr-only", id = "fs_desc", ""),
      tags$div(class = "fs-reader-actions",
        tags$a(class = "fs-btn-dl", id = "fs_dl", href = "#", download = NA, "Download sheet"),
        tags$a(class = "fs-btn-open", id = "fs_open", href = "#", target = "_blank",
          rel = "noopener", "Open in new tab")
      ),
      # Holder, not a live <iframe>: openFrame() creates the frame once and
      # then loads each sheet with location.replace(), so a sheet swap never
      # adds an entry to the session history this iframe shares with the site.
      tags$div(id = "fs_frame_holder")
    ),

    tags$div(id = "fs_live", class = "fs-sr-only", role = "status", `aria-live` = "polite")
  ),

  tags$script(HTML(paste0("window.__FS_DATA__ = ", fs_data_json, ";"))),

  tags$script(HTML("
    (function () {
      var home    = document.getElementById('fs_home');
      var area    = document.getElementById('fs_area');
      var reader  = document.getElementById('fs_reader');
      var live    = document.getElementById('fs_live');
      var areaH   = document.getElementById('fs_area_h');
      var areaSub = document.getElementById('fs_area_sub');
      var areaBody= document.getElementById('fs_area_body');
      var backBtn = document.getElementById('fs_back');
      var frameHolder = document.getElementById('fs_frame_holder');
      var homeH   = document.getElementById('fs_home_h');
      if (!home || !area || !reader) return;

      var DATA = window.__FS_DATA__ || {};
      var curCat      = null;   // slug of the area currently built / shown
      var lastAreaBtn = null;   // the .fs-vcard that opened the current area
      var lastRowBtn  = null;   // the .fs-row that opened the current reader

      function esc(s) { return String(s).replace(/&/g, '&amp;').replace(/</g, '&lt;').replace(/>/g, '&gt;'); }
      function att(s) { return esc(s).replace(/'/g, '&#39;'); }

      function showOnly(el) {
        home.hidden   = (el !== home);
        area.hidden   = (el !== area);
        reader.hidden = (el !== reader);
        var wrap = document.querySelector('.fs-wrap');
        if (wrap && wrap.scrollIntoView) wrap.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' });
        else window.scrollTo(0, 0);
      }

      function focusEl(el) { if (el && el.focus) el.focus(); }

      function buildArea(slug) {
        var a = DATA[slug];
        if (!a) return;
        curCat = slug;
        var n = 0;
        a.clusters.forEach(function (c) { n += c.sheets.length; });
        areaH.textContent = a.name;
        areaSub.textContent = n + ' fact sheets' +
          (a.clusters.length > 1 ? ', in ' + a.clusters.length + ' groups' : '');
        backBtn.textContent = '← Back to ' + a.name;
        backBtn.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Back to ' + a.name);
        if (areaBody.getAttribute('data-cat') === slug) return;  // already built

        var html = '';
        a.clusters.forEach(function (cl, i) {
          var clId = 'fs_cl_' + slug + '_' + i;
          html += `<h2 class='fs-cluster' id='${clId}'>${esc(cl.name)}</h2>`;
          html += `<ul class='fs-rows' role='list' aria-labelledby='${clId}'>`;
          cl.sheets.forEach(function (s) {
            html +=
              `<li><button type='button' class='fs-row'` +
              ` data-file='${att(s.file)}' data-title='${att(s.title)}'` +
              ` data-sub='${att(s.sub)}' data-desc='${att(s.desc)}' data-cat='${slug}'>` +
              `<span class='fs-row-x'>` +
              `<span class='fs-row-t'>${esc(s.title)}</span>` +
              `<span class='fs-row-d'>${esc(s.desc)}</span></span>` +
              `<span class='fs-row-go' aria-hidden='true'>&rarr;</span></button></li>`;
          });
          html += `</ul>`;
        });
        areaBody.innerHTML = html;
        areaBody.setAttribute('data-cat', slug);
        Array.prototype.forEach.call(areaBody.querySelectorAll('.fs-row'), function (btn) {
          btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            lastRowBtn = btn;
            showReader({ file:  btn.getAttribute('data-file'),
                         title: btn.getAttribute('data-title'),
                         sub:   btn.getAttribute('data-sub'),
                         desc:  btn.getAttribute('data-desc') });
          });
        });
      }

      function openFrame(st) {
        var url = 'factsheets/' + st.file;
        document.getElementById('fs_title').textContent = st.title;
        document.getElementById('fs_desc').textContent  = st.sub + '. ' + st.desc;

        var dl = document.getElementById('fs_dl');
        dl.href = url; dl.setAttribute('download', st.file);
        dl.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Download the ' + st.title + ' fact sheet');

        var op = document.getElementById('fs_open');
        op.href = url;
        op.setAttribute('aria-label', 'Open the ' + st.title + ' fact sheet in a new tab');

        // Load the sheet with location.replace(), never by pushing a new src:
        // this sub-app runs in an iframe whose session history is shared with
        // the surrounding site, so a pushed document navigation would add an
        // entry there. The first sheet gets a fresh element (its initial load
        // is a replace); later sheets reuse it via location.replace().
        var current = frameHolder.firstElementChild;
        if (!current) {
          var f = document.createElement('iframe');
          f.id = 'fs_frame';
          f.src = url;
          f.setAttribute('loading', 'lazy');
          f.title = st.title + ' fact sheet';
          frameHolder.appendChild(f);
        } else {
          current.title = st.title + ' fact sheet';
          try { current.contentWindow.location.replace(url); }
          catch (e) { current.src = url; }
        }
      }

      // Screen navigation is a plain in-memory state machine. It deliberately
      // does NOT use the History API: this app is an iframe that shares its
      // session history with the surrounding flexdashboard site, so calling
      // history.back() here used to skip past the app's own entries and land
      // on another site tab (e.g. the Scorecard). The browser / device Back
      // button now leaves the Fact Sheets tab, the same as every other tab.
      function showHome() {
        showOnly(home);
        focusEl(lastAreaBtn || homeH);
        lastAreaBtn = null; lastRowBtn = null;
        live.textContent = 'Fact Sheets home.';
      }

      function showArea(slug, forward) {
        buildArea(slug);
        showOnly(area);
        if (forward) focusEl(areaH);
        else { focusEl(lastRowBtn && area.contains(lastRowBtn) ? lastRowBtn : areaH); lastRowBtn = null; }
        live.textContent = areaSub.textContent + '.';
      }

      function showReader(st) {
        openFrame(st);
        showOnly(reader);
        focusEl(document.getElementById('fs_title'));
        live.textContent = st.title + ' fact sheet loaded.';
      }

      Array.prototype.forEach.call(document.querySelectorAll('.fs-vcard'), function (card) {
        card.addEventListener('click', function () {
          lastAreaBtn = card;
          showArea(card.getAttribute('data-cat'), true);
        });
      });
      document.getElementById('fs_area_back').addEventListener('click', showHome);
      backBtn.addEventListener('click', function () { showArea(curCat, false); });
    })();
  "))
  , adaparc_footer
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```

# ── Glossary data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Definitions for terms mapped to a variable are pulled from dict_vars
# (national_summary_text) so the glossary stays in sync with the data
# dictionary. Terms with no matching variable use a plain-language fallback.
gloss_def <- function(key, fallback = NA_character_) {
  v <- dict_vars %>%
    filter(var_readable == key, !is.na(national_summary_text)) %>%
    head(1) %>%
    pull(national_summary_text)
  if (length(v) == 0 || is.na(v) || !nzchar(trimws(v))) fallback else trimws(v)
}

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DISPLAY SETTINGS
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# One source for the two reader-facing display choices, palette and contrast.
# Phase 2 of docs/palette-v1-build-plan.qmd, added 2026-08-03.
#
# WHY NOT JUST READ input$access_map_palette. From phase 3 there are two
# controls bound to the same setting: this Help page dropdown and the floating
# Display panel reachable from every tab. Two inputs cannot both be "the"
# setting. Everything downstream reads display_settings() instead, so adding a
# third control later is one more observer and no change anywhere else.
#
# SESSION SCOPE, AND WHY IT MATTERS HERE. These are per-session reactives,
# deliberately not globals. scripts/palettes.R is sourced into the global
# environment, which is correct for constants, but a display setting held there
# would be shared by every visitor to the deployed app, and two readers would
# fight over each other's palette.

display_state <- reactiveValues(
  palette           = PALETTE_DEFAULT,
  contrast          = CONTRAST_DEFAULT,
  # TRUE once the URL has been read and found to carry an explicit ?contrast=.
  # Only the prefers-contrast observer reads it, to know whether to stand down.
  contrast_from_url = FALSE
)

# The single source. Every consumer reads from here, never from an input id.
display_settings <- reactive({
  list(
    palette  = pal_id(display_state$palette),
    contrast = pal_contrast_mode(display_state$contrast)
  )
})

# Write a setting, keep every bound control in step, and mirror it into the URL
# so a reader can bookmark or share the view they configured.
#
# mode = "replace" rather than "push": changing palette three times should not
# put three entries in the reader's back button.
#
# The early return on "nothing changed" is what stops the loop between this and
# the dropdown observer below, which fires again when updateSelectInput lands.
set_display_settings <- function(palette = NULL, contrast = NULL,
                                 announce = TRUE) {
  changed <- character(0)

  if (!is.null(palette)) {
    p <- pal_id(palette)
    if (!identical(p, display_state$palette)) {
      display_state$palette <- p
      changed <- c(changed, "palette")
    }
  }
  if (!is.null(contrast)) {
    k <- pal_contrast_mode(contrast)
    if (!identical(k, display_state$contrast)) {
      display_state$contrast <- k
      changed <- c(changed, "contrast")
    }
  }
  if (!length(changed)) return(invisible(FALSE))

  updateSelectInput(
    session  = getDefaultReactiveDomain(),
    inputId  = "access_map_palette",
    selected = display_state$palette
  )
  updateQueryString(
    paste0("?palette=",   display_state$palette,
           "&contrast=",  display_state$contrast),
    mode = "replace"
  )
  push_display_panel(announce = if (announce) changed else character(0))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Push the FULL state to the floating Display panel in www/cssloaders.html.
#
# Full state, never a delta, so the panel and the Help page dropdown cannot
# drift apart: whatever R believes is what both controls show. The choices list
# travels with it so the panel's <option> list is built from
# map_palette_choices() rather than being a second hardcoded list of palettes.
#
# `announce` names which settings changed. The panel drops the sentence into an
# aria-live region, so a screen reader user learns the setting took effect; a
# sighted reader sees the map recolour, and this is the equivalent.
push_display_panel <- function(announce = character(0)) {
  sess <- getDefaultReactiveDomain()
  if (is.null(sess)) return(invisible(FALSE))

  choices <- map_palette_choices()      # label -> id
  ids     <- unname(choices)
  labels  <- names(choices)
  pal_lab <- labels[match(display_state$palette, ids)]
  high    <- identical(display_state$contrast, "high")

  said <- character(0)
  if ("palette" %in% announce) {
    said <- c(said, paste0("Map color palette set to ", pal_lab, "."))
  }
  if ("contrast" %in% announce) {
    said <- c(said, if (high)
      "High contrast turned on." else "High contrast turned off.")
  }

  # Say plainly that high contrast has taken the palette over. Without this the
  # selector reads "Cividis" while the map is black and white, which looks like
  # a bug rather than a setting.
  note <- map_palette_note(display_state$palette)
  if (high) {
    note <- paste(note,
                  "High contrast is on, so maps are currently drawn in",
                  "Grayscale. Turning it off restores this palette.")
  }

  # Empty string, not NULL, for `announce`. A NULL in an R list serialises to a
  # JSON empty object, which is TRUTHY in JavaScript, and the live region would
  # end up announcing "[object Object]".
  sess$sendCustomMessage("adaparcDisplaySync", list(
    choices  = lapply(seq_along(ids),
                      function(i) list(id = ids[i], label = labels[i])),
    palette  = display_state$palette,
    contrast = display_state$contrast,
    note     = note,
    announce = paste(said, collapse = " "),
    # Phase 4.3. The generated :root block travels with the state that produced
    # it, in the same message, so the tokens and the data-adaparc-contrast hook
    # in www/styles.css cannot end up describing different modes. This is why
    # it is not a separate shinyjs::runjs() call: two channels would be two
    # chances to arrive out of order.
    css      = pal_css_rules(display_state$palette, display_state$contrast)
  ))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# Read the settings out of the URL once, on load, so ?palette=cividis_r or
# ?contrast=high arrives already applied. Unknown or misspelled values are
# absorbed by pal_id() and pal_contrast_mode(); a wrong colour is recoverable
# and a blank map is not.
#
# The unconditional push at the end used to be what populated the panel on a
# cold load. It is now a belt-and-braces second chance rather than the
# mechanism, because it fires on the session's first flush and could beat the
# browser's registration of the 'adaparcDisplaySync' handler, in which case
# Shiny discards the message and the panel's select stays empty. The panel now
# asks for its own state; see the display_panel_ready observer below. This push
# is kept because when it does win the race it saves a round trip, and when it
# loses it costs nothing. Silent either way: nothing has changed from the
# reader's point of view, so there is nothing to announce.
observeEvent(TRUE, {
  sess <- getDefaultReactiveDomain()
  if (is.null(sess)) return()
  qs <- parseQueryString(sess$clientData$url_search)
  # Recorded so the operating-system preference below knows to stand down. An
  # explicit ?contrast= in the URL is the reader saying what they want for THIS
  # view, and it outranks a machine-wide default.
  display_state$contrast_from_url <- !is.null(qs$contrast)
  if (!is.null(qs$palette) || !is.null(qs$contrast)) {
    set_display_settings(palette = qs$palette, contrast = qs$contrast,
                         announce = FALSE)
  }
  push_display_panel()
}, once = TRUE)

# Phase 1.1 of docs/palette-v2-build-plan.qmd, 2026-08-03. The other half of
# the handshake. The floating panel sets this input once it has registered its
# custom message handler and the websocket is up; R replies with the full
# state, exactly as push_display_panel() sends it anywhere else.
#
# WHY THE ASK COMES FROM THE BROWSER. Shiny drops a custom message SILENTLY
# when nothing is listening for its name. Only the browser knows when it has
# finished listening, so only the browser can say when it is safe to send. The
# server cannot detect the failure and cannot retry on a condition it cannot
# observe.
#
# NOT once = TRUE. A reconnecting session re-registers the handler and asks
# again, and the panel would otherwise come back empty for the rest of the
# visit. push_display_panel() is idempotent, and the panel's applyState()
# rebuilds the option list only when it actually differs, so an extra push
# costs one message and disturbs nothing the reader is looking at.
#
# Silent. This is a delivery mechanism, not a setting change, and the live
# region should not announce a palette the reader did not choose.
observeEvent(input$display_panel_ready, {
  push_display_panel()
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

# 4.5. Honour `prefers-contrast: more` on a cold load, so a reader who has
# already configured their machine does not have to find the panel.
#
# WHY THIS COMES FROM THE BROWSER RATHER THAN A CSS MEDIA QUERY. A media query
# would restyle the chrome but leave the maps on the reader's chosen palette,
# because those are ggplot and leaflet fills chosen in R and baked into the
# output. The whole point of routing everything through display_settings() is
# that the two cannot disagree, so the preference is read once in JavaScript and
# applied as a setting like any other.
#
# Read ONCE, at connect, and never again. Watching the media query live would
# mean a reader who turns high contrast off in the panel gets it turned back on
# by their operating system, which is the machine overruling the person.
observeEvent(input$display_os_prefers_contrast, {
  if (isTRUE(display_state$contrast_from_url)) return()
  if (!isTRUE(input$display_os_prefers_contrast)) return()
  set_display_settings(contrast = "high", announce = FALSE)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE, once = TRUE)

# ── The two controls ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Both are CONTROLS over the setting, not the setting. Each one only ever calls
# set_display_settings(); neither reads the other, and neither is authoritative.
# Adding a third is one more observer here and no change anywhere else.
#
# ignoreInit on the Help dropdown so the first flush does not write a query
# string onto a URL the reader never touched. The panel inputs need no such
# guard, because they are only ever set from a real change event in the browser.
observeEvent(input$access_map_palette, {
  set_display_settings(palette = input$access_map_palette)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE)

observeEvent(input$display_panel_palette, {
  set_display_settings(palette = input$display_panel_palette)
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE)

observeEvent(input$display_panel_contrast, {
  set_display_settings(
    contrast = if (isTRUE(input$display_panel_contrast)) "high" else "standard"
  )
}, ignoreInit = TRUE, ignoreNULL = TRUE)


# ── Reactive palette selection ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Returns a colorRampPalette FUNCTION rather than a colour vector, because both
# consumers (render_national_map() in scripts/functions.R and city_map_colors()
# below) already branch on is.function(). Keeping that contract means this swap
# needed no change in either consumer.
#
# pal_effective_fill_id() is where high contrast overrides the reader's palette
# with High Contrast Mono. It lives in scripts/palettes.R and is the same helper
# pal_css_vars() calls, so the maps and the stylesheet cannot end up disagreeing
# about what high contrast means.
access_map_fill_id <- reactive({
  ds <- display_settings()
  pal_effective_fill_id(ds$palette, ds$contrast)
})

access_map_palette_selected <- reactive({
  colorRampPalette(pal_fill(4, access_map_fill_id()))
})

# No-data fill for the currently selected palette. Per-palette, not global:
# High Contrast Mono spans pure white to pure black, so the shared grey would be
# indistinguishable from its lightest band. See the NO-DATA note in palettes.R.
access_map_na_selected <- reactive({
  pal_na(access_map_fill_id())
})

# Description of the selected palette, shown under the dropdown. This reports
# what the READER CHOSE, not the effective fill, so a high contrast reader still
# sees the description of the palette they will get back when they turn it off.
output$access_map_palette_note <- renderUI({
  tags$p(class = "help-palette-note",
         tags$strong("About this palette: "),
         map_palette_note(display_settings()$palette))
})

# Glossary CSV download (content built from glossary_df, so the file
# always matches the definition list shown on the Help page).
output$download_glossary <- downloadHandler(
  filename = function() "ADAPARC_Glossary.csv",
  content  = function(file) {
    readr::write_csv(glossary_df, file)
  }
)
```
